name: 90/90 Hold
desc: A seated hip mobility hold: both knees are bent to about 90 degrees, one leg in front of you and turned out, the other out to the side and turned in. Holding the position with your trunk upright stretches the outer hip of the front leg and the front of the hip of the back leg.
steps: Sit on the floor and bend your front leg in front of you so your shin runs across your body and your knee is bent to about 90 degrees.
Place your back leg out to the side with that knee also bent to about 90 degrees, shin pointing back.
Put your hands on the floor beside your hips for support.
Sit up tall, with your chest lifted and both sitting bones as close to the floor as you can manage.
Hold the position, breathing slowly, feeling the stretch in the outer hip of the front leg and the front of the hip of the back leg.
Hold for the planned time, then switch the legs and hold on the other side.
tips: Keep the trunk upright; slumping takes the stretch out of the hips.
If the hips are tight, keep more weight on your hands or sit on a folded towel until you can sit taller.
Ease into the stretch and do not force the knees down; the position should feel strong, not painful.

name: 90/90 Switch
desc: A hip-mobility drill in which you sit with both knees bent at right angles and rotate your legs from one side to the other, keeping the 90/90 position on each side. It trains the internal and external rotation of both hips as you switch.
steps: Sit on the floor with the front knee bent at 90 degrees and the back knee bent at 90 degrees, and place your hands behind you for support.
Sit tall and keep your trunk upright.
Lift both knees slightly and rotate your legs to the other side in a controlled movement, so that the front leg becomes the back leg.
Settle into the 90/90 position on the new side, using your hands for balance.
Switch back to the first side, and repeat for the planned repetitions.
Keep the movement slow and smooth, without forcing the hips.
tips: Keep your trunk tall; leaning back too far takes the work out of the hips.
Do the 90/90 hold first if you cannot reach the position on both sides.
Move slowly and stop if you feel pinching in the hip or pain in the knee.

name: Air Bike
desc: A full-body conditioning exercise on the air bike, combining pedaling with an arm push-pull for sustained power output.
steps: Sit on the air bike and grip the moving handles.
Place your feet on the pedals and brace your core.
Push and pull the handles while pedaling at a steady pace.
Drive with both arms and legs to maintain power output.
Continue for the desired duration or distance.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid slumping over the handles.
Breathe rhythmically to sustain effort over longer intervals.
Pull the handles with your back, not just your arms.

name: Archer Pull Ups
desc: A unilateral pull-up shifting the body toward one hand while the other arm stays straight, building single-arm pulling strength.
steps: Grip the bar wider than shoulder width with palms facing away.
Pull yourself up while shifting your body toward one hand.
Keep the opposite arm straight as a support.
Lower yourself under control back to the hang.
Alternate sides each rep or complete reps on one side first.
tips: Keep the straight arm fully extended and use it only as a guide.
Pull your chin toward the working hand, not straight up.
Master wide-grip pull-ups before progressing to archers.

name: Archer Push Ups
desc: A wide push-up lowering toward one hand while the opposite arm stays straight, loading one side at a time.
steps: Set up in a wide push-up position with arms straight.
Lower yourself toward one hand while keeping the other arm straight.
Keep your core tight and body in a straight line.
Press back up to the start position.
Alternate sides each rep for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your hips square to the floor as you shift sideways.
Let the straight arm assist as little as possible.
Start from wide push-ups and shift a little further each session.

name: Arnold Press
desc: An overhead press variation rotating the palms from facing the body to facing forward, working the front and side deltoids.
steps: Hold a pair of dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing you.
Press the dumbbells overhead while rotating your palms to face forward.
Fully extend your arms at the top without locking the elbows.
Reverse the motion and rotate back to the start.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Time the palm rotation evenly throughout the press, not all at once.
Avoid arching your lower back as the weight goes overhead.
Use a lighter load than a standard press to control the rotation.

name: Machine Assisted Dips
desc: A beginner-friendly dip performed on an assisted machine that offsets body weight, training the chest and triceps.
steps: Step onto the assisted dip machine with knees on the pad.
Grip the parallel bars and support your weight with straight arms.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until shoulders are below elbows.
Press back up to the start position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your elbows tracking back rather than flaring out wide.
Stop the descent if you feel pinching in the shoulders.
Reduce the assistance gradually as pressing strength improves.

name: Assisted Pull Ups
desc: A machine-assisted pull-up reducing the effective body weight, allowing beginners to train the lats through a full range.
steps: Place your knees on the assisted pull-up machine pad.
Grip the bar with palms facing away, slightly wider than shoulders.
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down.
Lower yourself under control to a full hang.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Pull your shoulder blades down before bending your arms.
Avoid swinging or using momentum from the knee pad.
Decrease the assistance over time to progress toward unassisted reps.

name: Back Extension
desc: An isolation movement targeting the lower back erector spinae on a hyperextension bench.
steps: Lie face down on a hyperextension bench with hips at the pad edge.
Lower your upper body toward the floor.
Raise your torso back up until your body is straight.
Repeat.
tips: Keep movements controlled.
Do not hyperextend beyond neutral spine.

name: Back Lever
desc: An advanced gymnastic isometric: hanging from a bar, the body is held horizontal and face-down in a straight line, demanding total-body tension through the lats, core, and posterior chain.
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip and rotate backward through the arms until inverted.
Lower the body forward and down until it is horizontal, facing the floor.
Keep the arms straight and the whole body in one rigid line from head to heels.
Brace the core and squeeze the glutes so the hips and shoulders do not sag.
Hold for time, then rotate back up under control.
tips: Build up with tucked and one-leg progressions before the full straight-body lever.
Depress and retract the shoulder blades to protect the shoulders.
Stay rigid -- any pike or arch collapses the hold.

name: Balance Dome Crunch
desc: A crunch done lying with your lower back on the domed side of a balance dome. The dome lets you start the curl from a slightly extended position, which lengthens the abdominals, and its instability makes the trunk work to keep you steady.
steps: Place the balance dome on the floor with the domed side up and sit on it, then lie back so your lower back rests on the dome.
Bend your knees and place your feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart.
Put your hands behind your head with your elbows wide, without pulling on your neck.
Curl your shoulders and upper back up toward your hips by shortening the distance between your ribs and your pelvis.
Pause briefly at the top and keep your lower back on the dome.
Lower back slowly to the start and repeat for the planned repetitions.
tips: Lead with the ribcage rather than the head; your hands only support your head.
Do not let the dome roll away; keep your feet planted and your hips still.
Start with a small range and extend further back over the dome as your control improves.

name: Balance Dome Glute Bridge
desc: A glute bridge with both feet on a balance dome: lying on your back with your heels or soles on the domed top, you lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees. The unstable surface makes the glutes and hamstrings work harder to keep the hips level.
steps: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and place both feet on the top of a balance dome with the domed side up.
Rest your arms flat on the floor beside you with your palms down.
Brace your trunk and press through your feet to lift your hips off the floor.
Raise your hips until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top and keep your hips level while the dome moves under your feet.
Lower your hips slowly to the floor and repeat for the planned repetitions.
tips: Press your whole foot into the dome rather than only the heel, which keeps the surface steadier.
Do not arch your lower back at the top; finish the lift with your glutes.
Master the floor glute bridge first and move your feet closer to the dome only when you can keep your hips level.

name: Balance Dome Plank
desc: A forearm plank with the elbows on a balance dome. The unstable surface makes the shoulders and the whole trunk work harder to keep the body in a straight line from head to heels.
steps: Place the balance dome on a flat floor with the domed side up and kneel behind it.
Put your forearms on the dome with your elbows under your shoulders.
Step your feet back into a plank with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your abdominals, keeping your neck long.
Hold the position for the planned time while the dome moves under you.
Lower your knees to the floor to finish.
tips: Do not let your hips sag or pike up; a straight line from head to heels is the target.
Press your forearms into the dome and keep your shoulders away from your ears.
Make it easier by widening your feet, or harder by bringing them closer together.

name: Balance Dome Push-Up
desc: A push-up with the hands on a balance dome turned flat side up. The dome tilts under your hands, so the chest, shoulders and triceps press you up while the shoulder stabilisers and the trunk keep you steady.
steps: Turn the balance dome over so that its flat platform faces up, and place your hands on the platform at about shoulder-width.
Step your feet back into a high plank with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your trunk and lower your chest toward the platform by bending your elbows.
Lower until your chest is just above the platform, keeping your elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Press the platform away to straighten your arms, keeping the dome as level as you can.
Repeat for the planned repetitions.
tips: Do plain push-ups first; the dome adds instability to a movement you should already control.
Keep your hips level and do not let the dome tilt to one side; look slightly ahead of your hands.
Place the dome on a non-slip floor and make sure the platform is flat before you put your weight on it.

name: Balance Dome Single-Leg Stand
desc: A balance hold on one leg on a balance dome, with the other knee lifted in front of you. The ankle, calf and hip muscles of the standing leg constantly adjust to the tilting surface, which makes it a demanding balance and rehabilitation exercise.
steps: Place the balance dome on a flat floor with the domed side up, next to a wall or a sturdy support.
Step onto the middle of the dome with one foot and stand tall with your knee slightly bent.
Shift your weight onto that leg and lift the other knee in front of you until the thigh is about hip height.
Keep your hips level, your chest tall and your eyes on a fixed point ahead.
Hold for the planned time, letting your ankle and calf make small corrections.
Lower the foot, rest and repeat on the other leg.
tips: Learn the two-foot balance dome stand first and keep a wall within reach.
Press the whole foot into the dome and let your toes spread; do not grip the surface with them.
Do not look down at your feet; a fixed point ahead helps your balance.

name: Balance Dome Squat
desc: A bodyweight squat done standing on the domed side of a balance dome. The surface moves under your feet, so the quadriceps and glutes lower and lift the body while the ankles and trunk work to keep you balanced.
steps: Place the balance dome on a flat floor with the domed side up and step onto the middle of it with both feet, about hip-width apart.
Find your balance and reach your arms straight out in front of you.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, lowering until your thighs are close to parallel with the floor.
Keep your chest up and your knees in line with your toes.
Press through your whole foot to stand back up.
Repeat for the planned repetitions and step off one foot at a time.
tips: Do the balance dome stand and squat hold first; the moving squat adds change of position to an unstable surface.
Keep your weight spread over the whole foot; heels lifting or knees caving inward are signs the surface is too hard for now.
Hold a wall or a rack with one hand until the movement feels steady.

name: Balance Dome Squat Hold
desc: A static squat held on a balance dome: you stand on the domed top and lower into a partial squat with your arms reaching forward, then stay there while the unstable surface keeps shifting. The quadriceps and glutes hold the position and the ankles and trunk work to keep you balanced.
steps: Place the balance dome on a flat floor with the domed side up and step onto the middle of it with both feet, about hip-width apart.
Stand tall and find your balance before you start to squat.
Push your hips back and bend your knees until your thighs are close to parallel with the floor.
Reach your arms straight out in front of you to counterbalance and keep your chest up.
Hold the position for the planned time, keeping your knees in line with your toes.
Stand up slowly and step off one foot at a time.
tips: Master the plain balance dome stand first; the squat adds load to an unstable surface.
Spread your weight across the whole foot and do not let your heels lift or your knees cave inward.
Hold a wall or a rack with one hand while you learn the position.

name: Balance Dome Stand
desc: A balance hold on a balance dome, the half-sphere trainer with a flat base: you stand on its domed top with both feet and keep your body steady while the surface moves under you. The calves and the small muscles around the ankles work constantly to hold you upright.
steps: Place the balance dome on a flat floor with the domed side up and stand next to it.
Step onto the middle of the dome with one foot, then bring the other foot up beside it, about hip-width apart.
Stand tall with your arms relaxed at your sides and your knees slightly bent.
Keep your weight even across both feet and look at a point straight ahead.
Hold the position for the planned time, letting your ankles and calves make small corrections.
Step off one foot at a time to finish.
tips: Stand next to a wall or a sturdy support the first few times so you can steady yourself.
Grip the dome with the whole foot and keep your toes relaxed; clenching them makes the balance harder.
Do not stare at your feet; a fixed point ahead of you helps your balance.

name: Balance Dome Step-Up
desc: A single-leg step-up onto a balance dome: you place one foot on the domed top, stand up on it and then step back down. The surface tilts under your foot, so the quadriceps and glutes lift the body while the hips and ankle work to keep you steady.
steps: Stand facing the balance dome, placed domed side up on a flat floor.
Place one foot flat in the middle of the dome.
Press through the whole foot and straighten that leg to stand up on the dome, bringing your other foot beside it.
Stand tall for a moment and keep your weight centred over the dome.
Step back down with the other foot first, then the working foot.
Complete the planned repetitions on one leg, then switch legs.
tips: Put your foot in the middle of the dome; stepping near the edge makes it tip.
Push through the heel and the whole foot rather than hopping up from the back leg.
Hold a wall or a rack with one hand until you can step up and down smoothly.

name: Stability Ball Leg Curl
desc: A bodyweight hamstring curl using a stability ball, rolling the heels toward the glutes while bridging the hips.
steps: Lie face-up on the floor with your heels and lower calves on top of a stability ball, arms out for balance.
Press through the heels to raise your hips into a straight line from shoulders to ankles.
Keeping the hips up, bend the knees to roll the ball toward your glutes.
Extend the legs back out under control without dropping the hips.
Complete all reps, then lower the hips and step off the ball.
tips: Hips stay up for the whole set — this is a combo bridge plus curl.
Start with both feet; progress to single-leg when it becomes easy.

name: Ball Pike
desc: An advanced core exercise where the hips pike up while the feet roll a stability ball toward the chest.
steps: Place the shins on a stability ball and hands on the floor in a high plank.
Brace the core and keep the legs straight.
Pike the hips up, rolling the ball toward the chest as the body forms an inverted V.
Pause briefly at the top.
Roll the ball back out to the starting plank.
tips: Keep the legs straight throughout — no knee bend.
Move at the hips, not the lower back.
Build up with knee tucks first if the pike is too hard.

name: Band Assisted Pull Ups
desc: A pull-up variation using a resistance band for assistance, reducing the load to build toward unassisted reps.
steps: Loop a resistance band over the pull-up bar and step one foot into it.
Grip the bar with palms facing away, shoulder-width apart.
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down.
Lower yourself under control to a full hang.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Avoid letting the band's recoil bounce you out of the bottom.
Keep the banded foot steady so the band cannot slip off.
Progress to thinner bands as your pulling strength increases.

name: Band Pull Apart
desc: A high-volume rear delt and scapular retractor exercise performed by pulling a resistance band apart at shoulder height.
steps: Stand holding a light resistance band with both hands, arms extended straight in front at shoulder height.
Hands start shoulder-width apart, palms facing down.
Keeping arms straight, pull the band apart by driving the hands out to the sides.
Finish with the band touching your chest and the shoulder blades squeezed together.
Return slowly to the starting position and repeat.
tips: Lead the movement with the little fingers — this externally rotates the shoulders.
Use a band light enough to do 15–30 clean reps; this is a high-rep prehab exercise.

name: Banded Adductor Stretch
desc: A lying stretch that uses a band to guide one straight leg out to the side and lengthen the inner thigh.
steps: Lie on your back with a band looped around one foot.
Raise that leg and let it open out to the side.
Hold the band to control how far the leg lowers.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your hips flat and both glutes on the floor.
Stretch to mild tension, never to pain.

name: Banded Ankle Stretch
desc: A seated stretch that uses a band around the forefoot to flex the ankle and lengthen the calf.
steps: Sit with one leg extended and a band around the forefoot.
Hold the band in both hands.
Pull so the toes draw back toward your shin.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep the leg straight and relaxed.
Stretch to mild tension, never to pain.

name: Banded Calf Stretch
desc: A lying stretch that uses a band around the ball of the foot to flex the ankle and lengthen the calf.
steps: Lie on your back and loop a band around the ball of one foot.
Raise the leg and keep it fairly straight.
Pull the band so your toes draw back toward your shin.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep the pull steady, not jerky.
Keep the knee softly straight.

name: Banded Chest Stretch
desc: A standing stretch that opens the chest by holding a band behind the back and drawing the arms apart.
steps: Hold a band behind your back with both hands.
Straighten your arms and draw them apart.
Lift your chest and squeeze your shoulder blades.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Keep your shoulders down away from your ears.
Stretch to mild tension, never to pain.

name: Banded Clamshell
desc: A clamshell hip-abduction performed with a loop band wrapped above the knees. The band adds constant tension on the gluteus medius — a small, focused isolation drill for hip stability.
steps: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent to roughly 45 degrees, feet stacked.
Place a loop band around both legs above the knees.
Keep the feet pressed together and the pelvis stable — do not roll back as you move.
Open the top knee upward against the band, like a clamshell opening, until you feel the glute fire.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower under control to the start.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
tips: The pelvis stays stacked — the moment you start rocking back, the glute disengages.
Slow controlled tempo beats heavy band; this is a stability drill, not a strength PR.
If you cramp in the side of the hip, that is exactly the right muscle. Shorten the set.

name: Banded Figure-4 Stretch
desc: A lying glute stretch in a figure-4 position, using a band to draw both legs toward the chest.
steps: Lie on your back and cross one ankle over the opposite thigh.
Loop a band around the supporting thigh.
Pull both legs toward your chest with the band.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
Let the crossed knee fall open.

name: Banded Fire Hydrant
desc: This isolation exercise uses a loop band to target and strengthen the gluteus medius and maximus, improving hip abduction and stability.
steps: Place a loop band just above your knees and assume a quadruped position with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Keep your core engaged and back flat, maintaining a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Slowly lift one knee out to the side, keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees, until your thigh is parallel to the floor.
Hold briefly at the top, squeezing your glute, then slowly lower your leg back to the starting position with control.
Complete all repetitions on one side before switching to the other side.
tips: Focus on controlled movement; avoid using momentum to lift your leg.
Keep your hips stable and prevent your torso from rotating or leaning.
Ensure the band stays taut throughout the entire range of motion.

name: Banded Glute Bridge
desc: A glute bridge with a loop band placed above the knees. Driving the knees out against the band recruits the gluteus medius alongside the prime glute-max bridge — a cheap accessory that doubles as hip activation.
steps: Lie on your back with the knees bent and feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
Place a loop band around both legs just above the knees.
Press the lower back into the floor and brace the core.
Drive through the heels and squeeze the glutes to lift the hips into a bridge — keep the band tension by pushing the knees outward.
At the top, the body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees. Pause briefly.
Lower under control to the start and repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: The knees want to cave inward — that is the band telling you to push them out.
Stop the lift when your hips are level with your shoulders and knees; do not hyperextend the lower back.
Squeeze hard at the top — a fast, half-rep bridge feels easy because it is.

name: Banded Good Morning
desc: A hip-hinge with a loop band over the upper back, targeting the hamstrings and glutes.
steps: Stand on a loop band with both feet and pass it over the back of your neck.
Set feet hip-width with a soft bend in the knees.
Hinge at the hips, pushing them back with a flat back.
Lower until you feel a stretch in the hamstrings.
Drive the hips forward to return to standing.
tips: Move from the hips, not the lower back.
Keep the chest up and the back flat throughout.
Use a band light enough to allow full range of motion.

name: Banded Hamstring Stretch
desc: A lying stretch that uses a band around the foot to draw a straight leg toward the torso and lengthen the hamstring.
steps: Lie on your back and loop a band around one foot.
Raise that leg straight up, holding the band in both hands.
Gently pull the band to draw the leg toward you.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep the raised leg as straight as you can.
Keep the other leg flat on the floor.

name: Banded Hip Thrust
desc: This exercise uses a loop band to increase glute activation during a hip thrust, effectively targeting the gluteus maximus, hamstrings, and gluteus medius for improved lower body strength.
steps: Place a loop band just above your knees and sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench.
Bend your knees, plant your feet hip-width apart, and position the band to create tension.
Drive through your heels, extend your hips, and lift your glutes off the floor until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes forcefully at the top, ensuring your knees are pushed out against the band.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position with control.
tips: Maintain constant tension on the band throughout the movement.
Focus on a strong glute contraction at the peak of the thrust.
Keep your chin tucked and gaze forward to maintain a neutral spine.
Ensure your shins are vertical at the top of the movement.

name: Banded IT-Band Stretch
desc: A lying stretch that uses a band to draw one leg across the body and target the outer thigh and hip.
steps: Lie on your back with a band around one raised foot.
Hold the band with the opposite hand.
Draw the straight leg across your body toward the floor.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep both shoulders down on the floor.
Stop when you feel a stretch along the outer thigh.

name: Banded Kneeling Hip Thrust
desc: This exercise strengthens the glutes and hamstrings by driving the hips forward against band resistance from a kneeling position.
steps: Place a loop band just above your knees. Kneel on the floor with your torso upright and knees hip-width apart.
Lean slightly forward from your hips, keeping your back straight and core braced.
Initiate the movement by squeezing your glutes, driving your hips forward until your torso is upright.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top, maintaining tension on the band.
Slowly reverse the movement, controlling the band's resistance as you return to the starting position.
tips: Focus on a strong glute contraction at the top of the movement.
Keep your core engaged throughout to prevent arching your lower back.
Maintain constant tension on the band by pushing your knees slightly outwards.

name: Banded Lat Stretch
desc: A standing stretch that lengthens the lats by hinging forward while holding a band overhead under tension.
steps: Hold a band overhead with both hands under light tension.
Hinge forward at the hips with your arms reaching ahead.
Let your chest sink to lengthen the sides of your back.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Keep your arms straight and shoulders relaxed.
Relax and keep breathing throughout.

name: Banded Lateral Walk
desc: A side-stepping movement performed with a loop band wrapped above the knees or around the ankles. Constant abduction tension fires the gluteus medius — a staple warm-up and rehab drill for hip stability.
steps: Place a loop band around the legs above the knees (or around the ankles for a harder version).
Stand in a quarter-squat: feet shoulder-width, hips back, chest up, knees tracking over the toes.
Step one foot directly out to the side against the band tension.
Bring the trailing foot in toward the lead — keep tension on the band the entire time, do not let the feet snap together.
Continue side-stepping in one direction for the prescribed reps or distance, then reverse.
Stay low throughout; do not pop up between steps.
tips: Keep the toes pointing straight forward — do not let the lead foot turn out.
Hips stay level; do not rock side-to-side as you step.
If the knees cave inward, the band is too strong — drop to a lighter one.

name: Banded Rear Delt Stretch
desc: A standing stretch that targets the rear shoulder by pulling one arm across the body against band tension.
steps: Loop a band around one arm and hold the other end.
Draw that arm horizontally across your chest.
Use the band to deepen the pull gently.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep the working shoulder relaxed and down.
Relax and keep breathing throughout.

name: Banded Romanian Deadlift
desc: A Romanian deadlift using a loop band, ideal for warm-ups and learning the hip-hinge pattern.
steps: Stand on a loop band with both feet and grip the top of the band.
Set feet hip-width with a soft bend in the knees.
Hinge at the hips, sliding the hands down the legs.
Lower until you feel a stretch in the hamstrings.
Drive the hips forward to return to standing.
tips: Keep the band close to the legs throughout.
Stop at the bottom of your clean range — no rounded back.
The movement is a hinge, not a squat — knees barely bend.

name: Banded Seated Hip Abduction
desc: This isolation exercise targets the gluteus medius and maximus by externally rotating the hips against band resistance while seated.
steps: Sit on a bench or chair with a loop band around your knees.
Keep your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, and maintain an upright posture.
Push your knees outwards against the band, engaging your glutes.
Hold the peak contraction briefly, then slowly return your knees to the starting position.
Control the movement throughout the entire range of motion.
tips: Focus on squeezing your glutes to initiate the movement.
Avoid leaning back or using momentum; keep your torso stable.
Choose a band resistance that allows for controlled movement.
Maintain tension on the band even in the starting position.

name: Banded Shoulder Stretch
desc: A standing stretch that opens the shoulders and chest by holding a band behind the back, one hand high and one low.
steps: Hold a band behind your back, one hand high and one low.
Keep light tension in the band.
Open your chest and draw your shoulders gently back.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Keep your ribs down and avoid arching your back.
Move your hands farther apart to ease the stretch.

name: Banded Squat
desc: A bodyweight squat with a loop band above the knees to teach knees-out tracking.
steps: Place a loop band just above the knees.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
Push the knees out against the band as you squat down.
Descend until thighs are parallel or below.
Drive through the heels to stand back up.
tips: Push the knees out against the band the whole rep.
Keep the chest up and the back flat.
Do not let the knees collapse inward.

name: Banded Standing Leg Curl
desc: A standing hamstring curl using a loop band anchored around the ankle, useful for travel or as a low-load hamstring finisher.
steps: Loop a resistance band around one ankle and anchor the other end under your standing foot or a fixed point in front of you.
Stand tall, holding onto something for balance if needed, with a slight bend in the standing knee.
Curl the banded heel up and back toward your glute, keeping the thigh still.
Squeeze the hamstring at the top, then lower under control to a full stretch.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch legs.
tips: Keep the thigh stationary — only the lower leg should move.
Avoid swinging the hips to generate momentum.
Use a lighter band if you can't control the descent.

name: Banded Standing Hip Abduction
desc: This isolation exercise targets the gluteus medius and maximus, improving hip stability and strength by abducting the leg against band resistance.
steps: Place a loop band around your ankles or just above your knees.
Stand tall with a slight bend in your knees and brace your core.
Shift your weight onto one leg, maintaining a stable torso.
Slowly abduct the free leg out to the side, feeling the glute contract.
Control the movement as you return the leg to the starting position.
Complete all reps per side before switching.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning to the side.
Focus on a controlled movement, not momentum.
Ensure the band maintains tension throughout the entire range of motion.
Initiate the movement from your hip, not your foot.

name: Banded Standing Hip Adduction
desc: A standing hip adduction with a loop band, isolating the inner thigh adductors.
steps: Anchor a loop band to a sturdy upright at ankle height.
Step into the loop with the working leg facing the anchor side.
Stand a few feet away so the band has tension.
Sweep the working leg across the body toward the standing leg.
Return slowly to the start. Complete reps per side, then switch.
tips: Keep the standing leg slightly bent for stability.
Move only the working leg — torso stays still.
Control the eccentric for full adductor stretch.

name: Banded Sumo Walk
desc: A wide-stance lateral walk with a loop band around the lower legs, targeting the glute medius and maximus.
steps: Place a loop band around your lower legs, just above the ankles.
Drop into a quarter squat with feet wider than shoulder-width.
Step sideways in a wide stance, keeping tension on the band.
Bring the trailing foot in only partway so the band stays taut, and keep stepping for the prescribed distance before leading with the other leg.
Stay low throughout — do not stand up between steps.
tips: Keep tension on the band the entire set.
Stay in a quarter-squat — do not stand tall between steps.
Take small, controlled steps with toes pointed slightly out.

name: Banded Terminal Knee Extension
desc: An isolation drill that locks out the knee against band resistance, often used for VMO and knee rehab.
steps: Anchor a loop band to a sturdy upright at knee height.
Step into the loop so the band sits behind one knee.
Step back so the band pulls the knee into a slight bend.
Extend the knee fully against the band, contracting the quad.
Return slowly. Complete reps per side, then switch.
tips: Squeeze the quadriceps hard at full extension.
Keep the foot flat — do not lift the heel.
Move only at the knee — the hip stays still.

name: Banded Triceps Stretch
desc: A standing stretch that lengthens the triceps by reaching one hand behind the head against band tension.
steps: Hold a band that runs down your back, top hand behind your head.
Anchor the lower hand at your lower back.
Reach the top hand down to feel the triceps lengthen.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your head upright and ribs down.
Relax and keep breathing throughout.

name: Barbell Ab Rollout
desc: A kneeling ab rollout using a loaded barbell with plates, giving smoother rolling and adjustable load compared to an ab wheel.
steps: Load plates of equal size on both ends of a barbell and place it on the floor.
Kneel behind the bar and grip it shoulder-width, arms extended.
Brace the core hard, then roll the bar forward away from your body.
Go as far as you can keep a neutral spine — stop before the hips sag.
Pull the bar back to the starting position by contracting the abs and lats.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Start with small plates for a limited range; graduate to 45s for full rollouts.
The moment the lower back arches or drops, stop — you've exceeded your range.

name: Barbell Box Squat
desc: A back squat with a barbell in which you sit back onto a box or bench at the bottom, pause for a moment and stand up again. The box fixes the depth and teaches you to sit back into the hips, and the brief pause removes the rebound out of the bottom.
steps: Set a box or bench behind you at a height where your thighs end up about parallel to the floor when you sit on it.
Take the barbell on your upper back, step back and stand with your feet a little wider than shoulder-width.
Brace your trunk and push your hips back, then lower yourself under control toward the box.
Sit onto the box without dropping onto it, keeping your chest up and your shins close to vertical.
Pause briefly with your muscles still tight, without relaxing your back.
Drive through your whole foot to stand up, and repeat for the planned repetitions.
tips: Sit back rather than down; the box should be touched with your hips, not rested on with your weight.
Keep the torso tight in the pause; relaxing on the box is where most back injuries happen.
Use a box that cannot slide, and lower it as you progress until you can squat to full depth.

name: Barbell Bulgarian Split Squat
desc: A single-leg squat with the rear foot raised on a bench and a barbell held across the upper back. The heavy, unilateral load works the quadriceps and glutes of the front leg and challenges balance and hip mobility.
steps: Set a barbell across the upper back and stand about two feet in front of a flat bench, facing away from it.
Place the top of one foot on the bench behind you, with the front foot far enough forward to keep the shin close to vertical when you lower.
Brace the trunk and lower the back knee toward the floor by bending the front hip and knee.
Descend until the front thigh is about parallel to the floor, keeping the chest up.
Drive through the middle of the front foot to return to the start.
Complete the repetitions on one leg, then switch.
tips: Keep most of the weight on the front leg; the back foot is only there for balance.
Keep the front knee tracking over the toes and the torso upright.
Use a lighter load than in a regular back squat, and set up the bar and a safe way to drop it before you step into position.

name: Barbell Calf Raise
desc: A standing calf raise loaded with a barbell across the upper back, using a raised platform for a deeper heel stretch.
steps: Place a barbell across your upper back as in a squat.
Stand with the balls of your feet on a raised platform.
Push up onto your toes as high as possible.
Pause and squeeze your calves at the top.
Lower your heels below the platform and repeat.
tips: Avoid bouncing out of the bottom stretch position.
Keep your knees straight but not locked throughout the set.
Move slowly to stay balanced under the bar.

name: Barbell Front Raise
desc: An isolation exercise raising a barbell from the thighs to shoulder height, targeting the front deltoids.
steps: Stand holding a barbell with an overhand grip at thigh level.
Keep your arms straight and core braced.
Raise the barbell in front of you to shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower under control and repeat.
tips: Use a light weight to avoid swinging the bar up.
Avoid leaning back as the bar rises.
Keep your wrists neutral rather than letting them bend backward.

name: Barbell Glute Bridge
desc: A weighted glute bridge using a barbell for increased resistance.
steps: Lie on the floor with a barbell across your hips and knees bent.
Drive your hips up by squeezing your glutes.
Hold at the top with hips fully extended.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
tips: Drive through your heels rather than your toes.
Finish with your ribs down to avoid arching the lower back.
Keep your knees in line with your feet, not caving inward.

name: Barbell Isometric Squat Hold
desc: An isometric version of the barbell back squat: you squat down with the bar on your upper back and hold the bottom position. The quadriceps, glutes and the muscles that keep your back rigid stay under tension at the deepest, hardest point of the squat.
steps: Set the bar on your upper back, grip it just outside your shoulders and step back from the rack with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Take a big breath into your belly, brace your core and keep your chest tall.
Sit down and back until your thighs are about parallel to the floor or a little below, with your knees tracking over your toes.
Stop at the bottom and hold the position, with your weight over the middle of your feet.
Keep your back flat and your knees pushed out while you hold for the planned time.
Drive up through your feet to stand, then rack the bar.
tips: Use safety arms or pins set just below your bottom position, since a long hold at depth is tiring.
Choose a lighter bar than your working squat weight; holding for time is harder than it looks.
Keep the knees pushed out over the toes instead of letting them collapse inward as you tire.

name: Barbell Lunge
desc: A forward lunge with a barbell across the upper back, training the quads and glutes one leg at a time.
steps: Place a barbell across your upper back and stand tall.
Step forward with one leg into a long stride.
Lower your back knee toward the ground until your front thigh is parallel.
Drive through your front heel to return to standing.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Take a stride long enough that your front knee stays over your ankle.
Keep your torso upright and core braced under the bar.
Push the floor away through the front heel, not the toes.

name: Barbell Overhead Extension
desc: This isolation exercise effectively targets the triceps brachii by extending the elbows overhead, promoting muscle hypertrophy and strength.
steps: Load a barbell with an appropriate weight and stand or sit with a neutral spine.
Grip the barbell with an overhand, shoulder-width grip, and press it overhead.
Slowly lower the barbell behind your head by flexing your elbows, keeping your upper arms stable.
Extend your elbows to press the barbell back to the starting overhead position, squeezing your triceps.
Maintain control throughout the movement, avoiding momentum.
tips: Keep your elbows tucked in and pointing forward to maximize triceps engagement and protect your shoulders.
Control the eccentric (lowering) phase to enhance muscle tension and growth.
Avoid arching your lower back excessively; brace your core to maintain stability.

name: Barbell Preacher Curl
desc: This isolation exercise targets the biceps brachii and brachialis by fixing the upper arms on a preacher bench, minimizing momentum and maximizing tension.
steps: Sit on a preacher bench with your chest against the pad, gripping a barbell with an underhand, shoulder-width grip.
Position your upper arms firmly against the pad, ensuring your elbows are slightly bent at the start.
Curl the barbell upwards by contracting your biceps, keeping your upper arms stationary on the pad.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, focusing on peak contraction.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, controlling the eccentric phase.
Lower until your arms are almost fully extended to get a full stretch in the biceps.
tips: Maintain constant tension on the biceps throughout the entire range of motion.
Avoid lifting your elbows off the pad; this indicates you're using too much weight or momentum.
Lower the bar slowly and under control; the stretched bottom position is where the elbows are most exposed.
Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms to prevent strain.

name: Barbell Pullover
desc: A compound movement stretching and loading the lats and chest through a wide arc.
steps: Lie across a bench with a barbell held over your chest.
Lower the bar back over your head in an arc.
Pull it back to the start over your chest.
Repeat.
tips: Keep a slight bend in the elbows.
Engage the lats to drive the bar back.

name: Barbell Rear Delt Row
desc: A bent-over barbell row with flared elbows that shifts emphasis from the lats to the posterior deltoids and upper back.
steps: Hinge at the hips with a flat back until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Hold a barbell with an overhand, wider-than-shoulder-width grip, arms hanging.
Row the bar up toward your upper chest with the elbows flaring out to the sides.
Pause and squeeze the rear delts and upper back at the top.
Lower the bar under control and repeat.
tips: Pull with the elbows, not the hands — think of driving them up and out.
Use a lighter load than a standard row; the wide grip reduces leverage.

name: Barbell Reverse Lunge
desc: A barbell lunge stepping backward instead of forward, keeping the front shin vertical while loading the quads and glutes.
steps: Place a barbell across your upper back and stand tall.
Step one foot backward into a long stride.
Lower your back knee toward the ground under control.
Drive through your front heel to return to standing.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Step back far enough to keep your front shin close to vertical.
Lower the back knee straight down rather than leaning forward.
Keep your chest tall and hips square throughout.

name: Bent-Over Barbell Row
desc: A compound pulling movement that targets the upper and middle back.
steps: Hinge at the hips with a slight knee bend.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Pull the bar to your lower chest, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower the bar under control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your torso at roughly 45 degrees.
Do not use momentum to swing the weight.

name: Barbell Wrist Curl
desc: A barbell wrist curl that isolates the forearm flexors for grip and forearm size.
steps: Sit on a bench with forearms resting on the thighs, palms up.
Hold a barbell with hands shoulder-width, wrists hanging off the knees.
Let the bar roll down to the fingertips at the bottom.
Curl the bar up by flexing the wrists.
Lower under control.
tips: Move only at the wrist — keep the forearms still.
Roll the bar to the fingertips for full range.
Use a thumbless grip if it helps wrist comfort.

name: Barbell Zercher Hold
desc: A standing hold with a barbell cradled in the crooks of your elbows against your abdomen. The abs and the trunk stabilizers resist the pull of the bar, while the biceps and the upper back keep it close to your body.
steps: Set a barbell on a rack at about the height of your lower ribs and place the crooks of your elbows under the bar.
Fold your arms and clasp your hands together in front of your chest to lock the bar against your body.
Lift the bar off the rack and step back, standing with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Stand tall, brace your abs and keep your ribs down, so that the bar rests against your abdomen without pulling you forward.
Hold the position for the planned time, breathing slowly and keeping your elbows pressed together.
Return the bar to the rack, or lower it to the floor with control.
tips: Wrap a towel or a barbell pad around the bar, since it presses into the elbows and the abdomen.
Keep the bar close to your body and do not lean back to carry it; if you do, the weight is too heavy.
Start with a bar a little lighter than your Zercher squat load, since the bar rests on your arms for the whole hold.

name: Barbell Zercher Squat Hold
desc: An isometric version of the Zercher squat: you squat down with the barbell in the crooks of your elbows and hold the bottom position. The quadriceps, glutes and the trunk stay under tension at the deepest point, while the arms and upper back keep the bar close to you.
steps: Set a barbell on a rack at about the height of your lower ribs, place the crooks of your elbows under the bar and clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Lift the bar off the rack, step back and stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Brace your abs and keep your chest tall, then sit down and back until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Stop at the bottom and hold, with your elbows resting inside your knees and your knees pushed out over your toes.
Keep the bar close to your abdomen and your back straight while you hold for the planned time.
Drive up through your feet to stand and return the bar to the rack.
tips: Wrap a towel or a barbell pad around the bar, since it presses into the elbows and the abdomen.
Use safety pins set just below your bottom position, since a long hold at depth is tiring.
Keep the chest tall; if the bar pulls you forward and your back rounds, the weight is too heavy.

name: Battle Rope Double Slam
desc: A conditioning movement in which both rope ends are driven up and slammed down together, producing one large wave per rep instead of the alternating waves of the standard battle rope drill.
steps: Take one rope end in each hand and face the anchor, standing far enough back that the ropes have a slight slack.
Set your feet slightly wider than your hips and sit into a quarter squat with your chest up.
Swing both arms up together, letting the ropes rise in front of you as you extend through the hips.
Slam both ends down to the floor at the same time, hinging at the hips and driving through your lats.
Ride the rebound straight back into the next slam, keeping both arms moving in unison rather than alternating.
Keep slamming for the desired time or number of reps.
tips: Both arms move together — the moment they start alternating you are doing the standard wave drill, which is a different exercise.
Drive the slam with your hips and lats rather than your arms, or your shoulders will burn out long before your lungs do.
Stand at the right distance from the anchor: too close and the rope goes slack, too far and you cannot get a wave into it at all.

name: Battle Ropes
desc: A high-intensity conditioning movement using thick ropes, training the upper back, shoulders, and grip.
steps: Anchor the ropes to a fixed point and grab one end in each hand.
Step back so the ropes have moderate slack.
Drop into a quarter squat with feet shoulder-width.
Drive each arm up and down rapidly to send waves through the ropes.
Continue for the prescribed work interval.
tips: Stay in the quarter-squat the entire interval.
Drive force from the legs and hips, not just the arms.
Keep the waves consistent and tight.

name: Bear Crawl
desc: A quadruped bodyweight crawl on hands and toes with the knees hovering just off the floor, building shoulder stability and core control as you travel forward.
steps: Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Tuck your toes and lift your knees a few centimeters off the floor.
Keeping your back flat and hips low, step your right hand and left foot forward together.
Then move your left hand and right foot, crawling forward in a controlled rhythm.
Keep your core braced and your hips from swaying side to side.
tips: Move opposite hand and foot together, like an exaggerated crawl.
Keep your knees low and hips level — do not let them pop up or rock.

name: Bear Plank Hold
desc: A static core hold on hands and knees in which the knees hover just above the floor while the back stays flat. It trains the abdominals and shoulders to stabilise the trunk and is a stepping stone to the full plank.
steps: Start on hands and knees with the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
Tuck the toes under and brace the abdominals so the back is flat.
Press into the hands and lift the knees a couple of inches off the floor.
Hold the position with the hips level and the head in line with the spine.
Breathe steadily, then lower the knees to rest.
tips: Keep the knees close to the floor; lifting them higher turns the hold into a pike.
Spread the fingers and push the floor away so the shoulders do not collapse.
Keep the neck long and look at the floor slightly ahead of the hands.

name: Behind the Back Barbell Shrug
desc: A shrug variation with the barbell held behind the body, targeting the trapezius.
steps: Stand holding a barbell behind your back with an overhand grip.
Keep your arms straight and chest up.
Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Pause and squeeze at the top.
Lower under control and repeat.
tips: Lift straight up and down without rolling the shoulders.
Avoid bending your elbows to heave the weight higher.
Stand tall with a neutral neck and look straight ahead.

name: Behind-the-Neck Lat Pulldown
desc: A wide-grip lat pulldown taken behind the head, targeting the upper lats and traps — requires full overhead shoulder mobility.
steps: Sit at a lat pulldown station with thighs secured under the pad.
Grip the bar with a wide, overhand grip — wider than shoulder-width.
Keep the torso upright and tuck the chin slightly forward.
Pull the bar down behind the head until it touches the base of the neck.
Return under control to the full overhead stretch.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Only perform this if you have full, pain-free overhead shoulder mobility.
Use a moderate load — this is not a strength lift, it's a hypertrophy accessory.

name: Behind the Neck Press
desc: An overhead press performed with the barbell starting behind the neck, emphasizing the front and side deltoids.
steps: Sit or stand with a barbell resting on your upper traps behind your neck.
Grip the bar wider than shoulder width.
Press the bar straight up overhead until your arms are extended.
Lower the bar back to the starting position under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Lower the bar only as far as your shoulders allow comfortably.
Keep your forearms vertical under the bar throughout the press.
Brace your core to avoid arching the lower back overhead.

name: Behind-the-Neck Pull-Up
desc: A wide-grip pull-up pulled high enough that the bar passes behind the head at the top instead of under the chin, which forces the shoulders into end-range external rotation.
steps: Grip the pull-up bar with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width and hang at full arm extension with your legs together.
Keep your torso vertical rather than leaning back, and pull your elbows down and out to the sides.
Continue pulling until the bar passes behind your head and the back of your neck comes level with it, without letting the bar touch your neck.
Lower yourself under control back to a full dead hang, keeping your head still rather than letting it snap forward.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: This variation is widely discouraged. Finishing behind the head loads the shoulder at the end of its external rotation, where the joint has the least capacity to protect itself, and any contact between the bar and the neck puts that load through the cervical spine.

A standard or wide-grip pull-up trains the same muscles through the same shoulder range — nothing about back development requires the bar to travel behind the head, so there is no benefit here to trade the risk against.

If you perform it anyway, stop well short of touching the bar to your neck and leave it out entirely if you lack full pain-free overhead shoulder mobility or have any history of shoulder or neck problems.

name: Bench Adductor Stretch
desc: A standing stretch with one straight leg resting on a bench out to the side to lengthen the inner thigh.
steps: Stand side-on to a bench.
Rest one straight leg up on the bench out to the side.
Keep your torso upright and shift gently toward the bench.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep both legs straight.
Keep the standing foot pointing forward.

name: Bench Ankle Stretch
desc: A standing stretch with the foot flat on a bench, driving the knee forward over the toes to flex the ankle.
steps: Place one whole foot flat on top of a bench.
Keep your torso upright.
Drive that knee forward over your toes.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your heel down on the bench.
Move slowly and keep the foot flat.

name: Bench Bulgarian Split Stretch
desc: A split-stance stretch with the rear foot on a bench, sinking the hips to open the hip flexors and quad.
steps: Rest the top of your rear foot on a bench behind you.
Set the front foot flat and bend that knee.
Sink your hips straight down.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Hold a wall for balance if needed.
Keep your torso upright.

name: Bench Calf Stretch
desc: A standing stretch with the ball of the foot on a bench edge, dropping the heel to lengthen the calf.
steps: Place the ball of one foot on the edge of a bench.
Keep that knee straight.
Let your heel drop down below the toes.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Hold the bench or a wall for balance.
Keep the movement slow and controlled.

name: Bench Chest Stretch
desc: A kneeling stretch with the hands behind on a bench, sinking the hips to open the chest and shoulders.
steps: Kneel with your back to a bench.
Place both hands behind you on the edge of the bench.
Sink your hips down to open the chest.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Keep your shoulders down away from your ears.
Stretch to mild tension, never to pain.

name: Bench Child's Pose
desc: A kneeling stretch with the arms resting on a bench, sitting the hips back to lengthen the lats and lower back.
steps: Kneel on the floor in front of a bench.
Extend both arms forward and rest them on the bench.
Sit your hips back toward your heels and let the chest sink.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Keep your arms straight and relax your neck.
Relax and keep breathing throughout.

name: Bench Couch Stretch
desc: A deep quad and hip-flexor stretch with the rear shin running up the front of a bench.
steps: Kneel with your rear shin against the front of a bench.
Place the front foot flat on the floor.
Bring your torso upright until the front of the thigh stretches.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Squeeze the rear glute to protect your lower back.
Pad the rear knee on a cushion for comfort.

name: Bench Decline Plank Hold
desc: A plank with your hands on the floor and your feet on a bench behind you, so that your body slopes downward toward your hands. The raised feet shift more of your weight onto the shoulders and make the abdominal muscles work harder than in a normal plank.
steps: Place a bench behind you and put the tops of your feet on it, then put your hands on the floor under your shoulders with your arms straight.
Walk your hands to a position where your body is in one straight line from your head to your heels.
Squeeze your glutes, brace your abs and push the floor away so that your shoulders do not sink between your shoulder blades.
Keep your neck in line with your spine and look at the floor between your hands.
Hold the position for the planned time, breathing slowly.
Lower your knees to the floor and rest.
tips: Do not let the hips sag or rise above the line; stop the set when the line breaks.
Keep your hands directly under your shoulders so that the weight is carried by the skeleton, not by sore wrists.
Use a lower step if the bench is too high to keep a straight line.

name: Bench Dips
desc: A bodyweight pressing movement with hands on a bench behind the body, emphasizing the triceps.
steps: Sit on a bench and place your hands on the edge beside your hips.
Slide your hips off the bench with legs extended.
Lower your body by bending your elbows to 90 degrees.
Press through your palms to return to the start.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your hips close to the bench as you lower.
Avoid letting your shoulders roll forward at the bottom.
Bend your knees to make the movement easier.

name: Bench Figure-4 Glute Stretch
desc: A seated stretch on a bench with one ankle crossed over the knee, hinging forward to target the glute.
steps: Sit on the end of a bench.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Keep your back flat and hinge forward over the crossed leg.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Let the crossed knee fall open.
Hinge from the hips, keeping the chest open.

name: Bench Hamstring Stretch
desc: A standing stretch with the heel on a bench, hinging forward over the straight raised leg to lengthen the hamstring.
steps: Place one heel on a bench with that leg straight.
Stand tall on the supporting leg.
Hinge forward from the hips over the raised leg.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your back flat as you fold forward.
Keep the raised leg straight, toes up.

name: Bench Hollow Hold
desc: A static core hold performed lying on a flat bench: the arms reach overhead and the shoulders and straight legs are lifted into a shallow hollow shape while the lower back stays pressed into the bench.
steps: Lie on your back on a flat bench with the glutes and lower back on the pad and the legs extended.
Reach the arms overhead beside the ears.
Brace the abdominals and press the lower back into the bench.
Lift the shoulders and the straight legs a few inches to form a shallow hollow.
Hold the position while breathing steadily, then lower to rest.
tips: If the lower back arches off the pad, raise the legs higher or bend the knees slightly.
Keep the ribs pulled down and the neck relaxed.
Hold only as long as you can keep the lower back flat.

name: Bench Lat Stretch
desc: A kneeling stretch with the hands on a bench, sinking the chest toward the floor to lengthen the lats.
steps: Kneel on the floor in front of a bench.
Place both hands on top of the bench.
Sit your hips back and let your chest sink down.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Keep your arms straight and head between your arms.
Relax and keep breathing throughout.

name: Bench Leg Pull-In
desc: A supine core exercise on a flat bench, pulling the knees toward the chest to train the rectus abdominis.
steps: Lie on your back on a flat bench and grip the sides behind your head for support.
Extend your legs straight out with heels just above the bench surface.
Pull your knees toward your chest, lifting the hips slightly off the bench.
Extend the legs back out under control without letting the heels touch the bench.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the lower back pressed into the bench to reduce hip flexor dominance.
Control the eccentric; do not let gravity drop the legs.
Squeeze the abs at the top of each rep for a stronger contraction.

name: Bench Pull
desc: A rowing exercise performed lying face down on an elevated bench, eliminating body momentum to target the lats and rhomboids.
steps: Lie face down on an elevated bench with arms hanging straight down.
Grip a barbell or dumbbells below you.
Row the weight up to the underside of the bench.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Lower under control and repeat.
tips: Keep your chest glued to the bench to prevent cheating.
Reach a full stretch at the bottom before each pull.
Drive your elbows up and back rather than curling the weight.

name: Bent Arm Barbell Pullover
desc: A pullover variation performed with elbows bent, lowering a barbell behind the head to stretch the lats and chest.
steps: Lie on a bench holding a barbell above your chest with bent elbows.
Keep your elbows bent throughout the movement.
Lower the barbell behind your head in an arc.
Pull the barbell back over your chest using your lats.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your ribs down and avoid arching your lower back.
Limit the stretch to a range your shoulders can control.
Breathe in deeply as the bar lowers behind your head.

name: Bent-Arm EZ-Bar Pullover
desc: A bent-arm pullover on a flat bench using an EZ-bar — wrist-friendlier than the straight barbell version while keeping the deep lat and pec stretch.
steps: Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ-bar with a narrow overhand grip on the inner bends.
Start with the bar above your chest, elbows bent to roughly 90 degrees.
Keep the elbow angle fixed and lower the bar back in an arc overhead until a deep stretch is felt in the lats and pecs.
Pull the bar back over the chest along the same arc, without straightening the elbows.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: The elbow angle stays fixed — only the shoulder moves.
Lighter load than a straight-arm pullover: range is longer and leverage is weaker.
If the lower back arches, plant the feet more firmly and brace the abs.

name: Bent-Knee Copenhagen Raises
desc: A shorter-lever version of the Copenhagen plank raise. In a side plank with your top leg on a flat bench, you bend the knee of your lower leg and lift it up toward the bench, then lower it again. The inner thigh muscles and the obliques work as in the straight-leg version, with less load on the lower leg.
steps: Lie on your side next to a flat bench and place the inside of your top leg or foot on it, with the top knee slightly bent or straight.
Prop yourself up on the elbow of your lower arm, directly under your shoulder.
Lift your hips so that your body forms a straight line from your head to your top leg, and bend the knee of your lower leg under you.
Raise the bent lower knee up toward the bench, keeping your hips high.
Lower the knee slowly without letting your hips drop, and repeat for the planned repetitions.
Rest, then switch sides.
tips: Use this version to build up to the straight-leg Copenhagen raise; the bent knee shortens the lever and lowers the load.
Keep your hips high and your body in one line; dropping the hips takes the load off the inner thighs.
Move slowly and stop if you feel a sharp pull in the groin; the adductors need a gentle build-up.

name: Bicycle Crunch
desc: A dynamic crunch variation targeting both the rectus abdominis and obliques.
steps: Lie on your back with hands behind your head and legs raised.
Bring one knee toward your chest while rotating your torso to meet it with the opposite elbow.
Extend that leg while bringing the other knee in.
Continue alternating in a pedaling motion.
Repeat.
tips: Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands.
Lead the rotation with your shoulder, not your elbow.
Move slowly and deliberately rather than racing through reps.

name: Bird-Dog
desc: A core stability exercise extending opposite arm and leg to challenge the erector spinae and deep core.
steps: Start on all fours with a neutral spine.
Extend your right arm forward and left leg back simultaneously.
Hold for a moment, then return.
Repeat on the other side.
Alternate.
tips: Move slowly and with control.
Keep hips level throughout.

name: Bird Dog Hold
desc: A static core hold balancing on all fours with one arm and the opposite leg extended, training spinal stability.
steps: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Extend one arm forward and the opposite leg back.
Keep your core tight and body level.
Hold the position without rotating your torso.
Hold for time. Complete on one side, then switch.
tips: Reach long through your fingertips and heel in opposite directions.
Push the floor away with your supporting hand to stay stable.
Breathe steadily instead of holding your breath.

name: Boat Pose
desc: A seated balance on the sit bones with the legs lifted and the chest tall, holding a V shape that loads the hip flexors and the whole front of the trunk.
steps: Sit on the floor with the knees bent and the feet flat, hands resting behind the thighs.
Lean back until you balance just behind the sit bones and lift the chest so the spine stays long.
Lift the shins until they are parallel to the floor, then straighten the legs as far as the back stays flat.
Reach the arms forward beside the legs and hold the position for the prescribed time.
Lower the feet under control to finish.
tips: Keep the chest lifted; the moment the back rounds, bend the knees again.
Hold behind the thighs if the hamstrings limit you more than the core does.
Breathe steadily instead of bracing against a held breath.

name: Bodyweight Calf Raise
desc: A beginner-friendly calf raise using body weight only on flat ground, strengthening the gastrocnemius and soleus.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart on a flat surface.
Push up onto the balls of your feet as high as possible.
Squeeze your calves at the top.
Lower your heels back to the floor under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Use light fingertip support for balance if needed.
Control the lowering phase instead of dropping your heels quickly.
Keep your ankles from rolling outward as you rise.

name: Bodyweight Good Morning
desc: A bodyweight hip hinge with hands behind the head, strengthening the hamstrings and spinal erectors.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hands behind your head.
Keep a slight bend in your knees and brace your core.
Hinge at the hips and lower your torso toward parallel.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Push your hips back as if closing a door behind you.
Keep your spine neutral from head to tailbone throughout.
Stop the descent when your hamstrings reach their stretch limit.

name: Bodyweight Lateral Raise
desc: A shoulder isolation movement performed without equipment to develop lateral deltoid width.
steps: Stand upright with arms hanging at your sides.
Raise both arms out to the sides with a slight elbow bend until parallel with the floor.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired reps.
tips: Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders at the top.
Control the descent to maximize time under tension.

name: Bodyweight Overhead Press
desc: An unloaded standing overhead press: the arms press up from the shoulders until they are straight overhead, rehearsing the pressing pattern for the shoulders and triceps without any equipment.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your hands in loose fists at shoulder height, palms facing forward and elbows under the wrists.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your ribs stay down.
Press both arms straight up until the elbows are fully extended and the upper arms are beside your ears.
Lower your hands back to shoulder height under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Finish with your hands directly over your shoulders, not in front of your face.
Do not lean back or arch your lower back to get the arms higher.
Once the pattern feels smooth, hold light dumbbells or a band to add load.

name: Bodyweight Reverse Lunge
desc: A lunge variation using only body weight, stepping backward for better knee stability than a forward lunge.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step one leg back and lower your knee toward the floor.
Lower until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Push through your front heel to return to standing.
Repeat on both sides.
tips: No weight needed -- focus on balance and a controlled descent.
Keep your torso upright instead of leaning forward.
Step back far enough that your front knee stays behind your toes.

name: Bodyweight Squat
desc: A foundational lower-body exercise squatting with body weight only, developing the quadriceps, glutes, and basic movement mechanics.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended forward.
Sit back and down by bending your hips and knees.
Lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to return to standing.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your weight spread across your whole foot.
Track your knees in line with your toes.
Keep your chest up to avoid rounding the upper back.

name: Bow Pose
desc: A prone backbend in which the hands hold the ankles and the legs press away, lifting the chest and thighs off the floor and loading the whole back line.
steps: Lie face down with the arms beside the body and the forehead resting on the mat.
Bend the knees and take hold of the outside of both ankles.
Press the shins back into the hands so the chest and thighs lift away from the floor.
Hold the lifted position for the prescribed time, keeping the neck long and the gaze forward.
Release the ankles and lower down under control.
tips: Drive the lift from the legs pressing into the hands, not from pulling with the arms.
Keep the knees roughly hip-width apart rather than letting them splay.
If the shoulders feel pinched, lift less and keep the chest open instead.

name: Box Jump
desc: A plyometric jump from a quarter-squat onto a stable box, training lower-body power.
steps: Stand a foot in front of a sturdy box with feet shoulder-width.
Drop into a quarter-squat and swing the arms back.
Drive the arms up and explode off the floor onto the box.
Land softly with both feet flat and knees bent.
Step down — do not jump down — and reset.
tips: Always step down — repeated drop-landings stress the Achilles.
Land softly with the whole foot, knees tracking over the toes.
Pick a box height you can clear cleanly without piking the hips.

name: Box Squat
desc: A squat performed to a box or bench, which fixes the depth and teaches sitting back into the hips.
steps: Stand in front of a box or bench, feet shoulder-width apart, with your arms extended forward for balance.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, sitting back toward the box rather than straight down.
Touch the box lightly with your glutes without collapsing onto it.
Drive through your feet to stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Use a box height that lets your thighs reach about parallel to the floor and lower it as mobility improves.
Keep your weight through the middle of your feet — do not rock onto your toes.
Touch and go: fully relaxing onto the box loses core tension and stresses the spine.

name: Burpees
desc: A full-body conditioning movement combining a squat, plank, push-up, and jump.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down and place the hands on the floor in front of you.
Jump or step the feet back into a plank, then perform a push-up.
Jump or step the feet forward to the hands.
Stand up and jump explosively, reaching the arms overhead.
tips: Keep the back flat in the plank — do not let the hips sag.
Land softly from the jump.
Scale by stepping the feet back instead of jumping.

name: Butterfly Stretch
desc: A seated stretch for the inner thighs, pressing the soles of the feet together with the knees dropped out.
steps: Sit tall and press the soles of your feet together.
Let your knees drop out toward the floor.
Hold your feet and sit up tall.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Gently press the knees down with your elbows for more stretch.
Bring your heels closer to your body to increase intensity.

name: Cable Bent-Over Row
desc: A cable rowing variation providing constant tension throughout the movement.
steps: Attach a straight or V-bar to a low cable pulley.
Hinge at the hips with knees slightly bent.
Pull the handle toward your lower chest.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Lower with control and repeat.
tips: Hold the hinge position steady instead of standing up as you pull.
Keep your back flat from head to hips throughout.
Resist the cable's pull on the way back to full stretch.

name: Cable Chest Press
desc: A standing chest press on the cable machine, providing constant tension while the staggered stance demands core stability.
steps: Set the cables to chest height and face away from the machine.
Grip a handle in each hand and step forward into a staggered stance.
Press the handles forward until your arms are extended.
Squeeze your chest at the top.
Return under control and repeat.
tips: Press both handles evenly to avoid twisting your torso.
Brace your core against the backward pull of the stack.
Step forward enough that the cables stay taut throughout each rep.

name: Cable External Rotation
desc: A cable exercise rotating the forearm outward with the elbow pinned at the side, strengthening the rotator cuff's external rotators with the rear delts assisting.
steps: Set a cable pulley to elbow height and grip the handle.
Stand side-on to the machine with your working elbow bent at 90 degrees.
Keep your elbow glued to your side and rotate your forearm outward.
Pause at the end of the movement.
Return under control. Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Use a light weight to keep the rotation strict and controlled.
Keep your wrist straight and in line with your forearm.
Avoid shrugging your shoulder or twisting your torso during the movement.

name: Cable Front Raise
desc: An isolation exercise raising a cable handle to shoulder height, keeping constant tension on the front delt.
steps: Stand facing away from a low cable pulley with a handle attachment.
Hold the handle with arm extended at your thigh.
Raise your arm forward to shoulder height keeping it straight.
Pause at the top.
Lower under control and repeat.
tips: Avoid swinging or using momentum to lift the handle.
Keep your torso upright; do not lean back as the arm rises.
Brace your core and keep your wrist neutral throughout.

name: Cable Hammer Curl
desc: A cable curl using a rope attachment with a neutral grip to target the brachialis and brachioradialis with constant tension.
steps: Attach a rope to a low cable pulley and stand facing the machine.
Grip the rope with a neutral (hammer) grip, palms facing each other.
Curl the rope upward toward your shoulders, keeping elbows pinned at your sides.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.
Repeat for the desired reps.
tips: Keep your elbows stationary throughout the movement.
Pull the rope ends apart slightly at the top to increase contraction.
Avoid swinging the torso.

name: Cable Glute Kickback
desc: A cable isolation exercise for the glutes, extending the hip back against constant resistance.
steps: Attach an ankle cuff to a low cable pulley and fasten it around one ankle.
Stand facing the machine, holding the frame lightly for balance, and hinge slightly forward at the hips.
Kick the cuffed leg straight back, extending the hip fully while keeping the knee nearly straight.
Squeeze the glute at full hip extension, then return the foot slowly to the start.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.
tips: Lead with the heel to maximize glute activation over hamstrings.
Keep the hips square; avoid rotating the pelvis as the leg kicks back.
The movement comes entirely from the hip — keep the back and torso still.

name: Cable Pallof Press
desc: An anti-rotation core exercise in which a cable pulls you sideways while you press a handle straight out from your chest and refuse to let your torso turn.
steps: Set a cable at chest height and take the handle in both hands, standing side-on to the machine.
Step away until there is real tension on the cable, with your feet about shoulder-width apart and knees softly bent.
Bring the handle to the centre of your chest and brace your trunk and glutes.
Press the handle straight out in front of you until your arms are extended, resisting the pull that wants to rotate you toward the machine.
Hold the extended position for a moment, then bring the handle back to your chest under control.
Complete the desired reps, then turn around and repeat facing the other way.
tips: Nothing should rotate. If your shoulders turn toward the cable as you press, reduce the weight — the point is the rotation that does not happen.
The further you step from the machine, the longer the lever and the harder it gets, so you can change difficulty without touching the weight stack.
Keep your arms level with your chest and your shoulders down; letting the handle drift up turns it into a front raise.

name: Cable Pull-Through
