desc: A cable-resisted hip hinge performed facing away from a low pulley, loading the glutes and hamstrings without placing a bar across the spine.
steps: Attach a rope to the low pulley and stand facing away from the machine with the rope between the legs.
Step forward until the cable is taut, then brace the trunk and soften the knees.
Push the hips back while keeping the spine neutral and the arms long.
Drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to stand tall.
Reverse into the next hinge without letting the weight stack slam down.
tips: Think hips back and hips through; the arms only hold the rope.
Keep the shins nearly vertical so the movement stays a hinge rather than a squat.
Finish tall without leaning backwards at lockout.

name: Cable Reverse Fly
desc: A standing cable exercise for the rear deltoids: facing the space between two cable towers, you hold the opposite handles with the cables crossed in front of you and sweep your arms out and back until they are level with your shoulders. The cables keep tension on the back of the shoulders through the whole arc.
steps: Set both pulleys at about shoulder height and stand centred between the two cable towers.
Take the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left hand, so the cables cross in front of you.
Stand tall with your arms reaching forward at shoulder height and a slight bend in the elbows.
Sweep your arms out and back in a wide arc, leading with the elbows, until they are in line with your shoulders.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together briefly without arching your lower back.
Bring the handles back to the crossed start position slowly and repeat for the planned repetitions.
tips: Keep the elbows soft and fixed; bending and straightening them turns the fly into a row.
Keep your shoulders down and your neck relaxed so the rear deltoids do the work, not the upper trapezius.
Use a light weight and a slow return; the cables pull hardest at the end of the arc, so control that position.

name: Cable Tricep Kickback
desc: An isolation movement performed hinged forward, extending the elbow against cable resistance to work the triceps.
steps: Attach a handle to a low cable and hinge forward at the hips.
Tuck your upper arm against your side with elbow bent 90 degrees.
Extend your elbow to push the handle back behind you.
Squeeze your triceps at the end of the movement.
Return under control. Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Move only your forearm; keep the upper arm completely still.
Avoid rounding your back while holding the hinged position.
Use a light weight to reach full lockout without swinging.

name: Cable Upright Row
desc: An upright row performed with a cable for constant tension on the lateral deltoids and traps.
steps: Stand in front of a cable machine and grip a straight bar or rope at thigh height.
Pull the bar up toward your chin, leading with your elbows.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep elbows higher than your wrists.
Avoid shrugging excessively.

name: Cable Wrist Curl
desc: An isolation exercise for the forearm flexors: seated on a flat bench with your forearms resting on your thighs, you hold a short bar attached to a low cable pulley in front of you and curl it up by flexing your wrists. The thighs keep the forearms still, so only the wrists move.
steps: Attach a short straight bar to a low cable pulley and sit on a flat bench facing the pulley, feet flat on the floor.
Take the bar with an underhand grip, palms facing up, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Rest your forearms on your thighs so that your wrists and hands reach just past your knees.
Let the cable pull your wrists down until you feel a stretch in your forearms.
Curl the bar up by flexing your wrists, keeping your forearms on your thighs.
Lower the bar under control and repeat for the planned repetitions.
tips: Move only at the wrists; keep your forearms pressed against your thighs.
Perform the reps slowly to avoid straining your wrists.
Pause briefly at the top of each rep for a stronger contraction.

name: Calf Raise Hold
desc: An isometric calf exercise: you rise onto the balls of your feet with the knees straight and hold the top position. The gastrocnemius and the soleus stay under constant tension at the point where a calf raise is hardest, with no movement to hide behind.
steps: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart and your arms relaxed at your sides.
Push through the balls of your feet and rise onto your toes as high as you can.
Keep your knees straight and your weight over the middle of your feet, not rolling out to the little toes.
Stop at the top and hold the position, heels as high as possible.
Keep your hips level, your chest tall and your breathing slow while you hold for the planned time.
Lower your heels slowly to the floor and rest.
tips: Hold on to a wall or a rack with one hand if you wobble; the aim is the calf contraction, not the balance.
Do not let the heels sink during the hold; if they drop, end the set instead of bouncing back up.
Add a pair of dumbbells or a loaded backpack once you can hold bodyweight for a full minute.

name: Camel Pose
desc: A kneeling backbend that opens the front of the hips, the abdomen and the chest while the hands support the position on the heels or the lower back.
steps: Kneel with the knees hip-width apart and the hips stacked over the knees.
Place the hands on the back of the pelvis with the fingers pointing down and lift the chest.
Press the hips forward and arch back, reaching for the heels if the position stays comfortable.
Hold the pose for the prescribed time, keeping the neck in line with the spine.
Bring the hands back to the pelvis and come up chest-first.
tips: Keep the hips over the knees; letting them travel back turns the pose into a collapse.
Tuck the toes under and rest the hands on raised heels if the full reach is too deep.
Come out slowly: lifting the head first is what usually makes people dizzy.

name: Captain's Chair Knee Raise
desc: A bodyweight core exercise performed on a captain's chair that targets the lower abs and hip flexors.
steps: Position yourself in the captain's chair with your back flat against the pad and forearms on the armrests.
Let your legs hang straight down.
Engage your core and raise your knees toward your chest.
Hold briefly at the top, then lower slowly to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired reps.
tips: Avoid swinging the legs for momentum.
Exhale as you raise your knees.
Keep your back pressed against the pad throughout.

name: Captain's Chair Leg Raise
desc: A bodyweight core exercise on a captain's chair that targets the lower abs and hip flexors with straight legs for greater difficulty.
steps: Position yourself in the captain's chair with your back flat against the pad and forearms on the armrests.
Let your legs hang straight down.
Keeping your legs straight, raise them until parallel with the floor or higher.
Hold briefly at the top, then lower slowly.
Repeat for the desired reps.
tips: Keep your legs as straight as possible throughout.
Avoid swinging — control the movement with your core.
For less difficulty, bend the knees slightly.

name: Cat-Cow
desc: A kneeling flow that alternates between rounding the spine towards the ceiling and letting it sag while the chest opens, moving every segment of the back through its range.
steps: Start on all fours with the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
Exhale and round the spine towards the ceiling, tucking the tailbone and letting the head drop.
Inhale and reverse it: let the belly sink, lift the chest and tailbone, and look slightly forward.
Move between the two shapes slowly, one breath per position.
Finish in a neutral spine and sit back onto the heels.
tips: Let the breath set the tempo rather than rushing between the two positions.
Keep the hands pressing evenly so the shoulders do not collapse towards the floor.
Move the whole spine, including the neck, instead of hinging only at the lower back.

name: Cat Stretch
desc: A kneeling stretch that rounds the spine upward to lengthen the back muscles.
steps: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Round your spine up toward the ceiling.
Tuck your chin toward your chest.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Push the floor away with your hands to spread the shoulder blades.
Relax and keep breathing throughout.

name: Chair Pose
desc: A standing hold with the hips sunk back and the arms overhead, so the quadriceps and the upper back work isometrically against bodyweight.
steps: Stand with the feet together or hip-width apart and the weight in the heels.
Bend the knees and send the hips back as if sitting down onto a chair.
Raise the arms overhead beside the ears, keeping the ribs from flaring.
Hold the position for the prescribed time with the chest lifted and the knees tracking over the toes.
Press through the heels to stand back up.
tips: Keep enough weight in the heels that you could lift the toes.
Take the arms slightly forward if raising them fully makes the lower back arch.
Sink lower for more quadriceps work, but only while the heels stay down.

name: Cheat Curl
desc: A momentum-assisted bicep curl using slight hip drive on the way up and a slow, controlled lowering phase.
steps: Stand holding weight at thigh level with an underhand grip.
Use a slight hip drive to start the curl.
Curl the weight up toward your shoulders explosively.
Lower the weight slowly under control through the full range.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep the hip drive small so your biceps still do most of the work.
Avoid leaning back excessively to protect your lower back.
Keep your elbows close to your torso throughout the curl.

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
desc: A dumbbell row with chest support to eliminate lower back strain and isolate the back muscles.
steps: Lie face-down on an incline bench with dumbbells hanging beneath.
Row the dumbbells up to your sides.
Squeeze at the top, then lower.
Repeat.
tips: The chest support eliminates back fatigue.
Focus on squeezing the shoulder blades together.

name: Chest Supported Dumbbell Shrug
desc: A shrug performed face-down on an incline bench, the chest support isolating the traps and removing momentum.
steps: Set an incline bench to about 30 degrees.
Lie face down on the bench holding dumbbells at arm's length.
Shrug your shoulders up and back toward your ears.
Squeeze your upper traps at the top.
Lower under control and repeat.
tips: Shrug up and back toward your ears rather than straight up.
Keep your chest pinned to the pad so you cannot use body english.
Pause and squeeze at the top before lowering under control.

name: Chest-Supported Kettlebell Row
desc: This exercise targets your back muscles, primarily the latissimus dorsi and rhomboids, by rowing a kettlebell in each hand towards your hips while your torso is supported on an incline bench.
steps: Lie face down on an incline bench, allowing your arms to hang freely with a kettlebell in each hand.
Brace your core and retract your shoulder blades.
Pull the kettlebells towards your hips, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top, feeling the contraction in your back.
Slowly lower the kettlebells back to the starting position with control.
tips: Maintain a stable torso throughout the movement; avoid rocking.
Focus on initiating the pull with your back muscles, not just your arms.
Keep your elbows close to your body to emphasize the lats.

name: Chest-Supported Smith Machine Row
desc: A row performed against an inclined pad inside the Smith machine, where the chest support removes the lower back from the movement and the guided bar keeps the pull in one line.
steps: Set an incline bench inside the Smith machine facing the bar, and set the bar low enough that your arms hang straight when you lean on the pad.
Stand astride the bench with your feet planted and your chest resting against the top of the pad.
Take an overhand grip a little wider than shoulder-width and unhook the bar with your arms extended.
Pull the bar up to your lower chest, leading with your elbows and squeezing the shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower the bar under control until your arms are straight again, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your chest on the pad for every repetition. The moment you push off it to move the weight you have turned this back into a bent-over row and given up the reason for the setup.
Lead with the elbows and stop when they pass your torso. Pulling further only rolls the shoulders forward and the fixed bar path leaves nowhere for them to go.
Because your lower back is doing nothing here, this is the row to use on a day when a bent-over row is not an option -- match the weight to what your back can pull, not to what your legs could brace.

name: Child's Pose
desc: A kneeling rest stretch that lengthens the lats, lower back and shoulders with the arms reaching forward.
steps: Kneel and sit your hips back toward your heels.
Fold your torso forward over your thighs.
Reach both arms out long on the floor in front.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Spread your knees wider to rest your chest lower.
Relax and keep breathing throughout.

name: Chin Tuck Hold
desc: A static neck drill that retracts the head straight back to strengthen the deep neck flexors and counter forward-head posture.
steps: Stand or sit tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Pull your chin straight back, creating a double chin.
Keep your head level without tilting.
Hold the position for the desired duration.
Release and repeat for multiple sets.
tips: Imagine sliding your head back over your spine, not nodding down.
Keep your gaze level and your breathing relaxed.

name: Clamshells
desc: A side-lying hip exercise opening the top knee against gravity to activate the gluteus medius.
steps: Lie on your side with knees bent and stacked on top of each other.
Keep your feet together and hips stacked.
Open your top knee toward the ceiling without rotating your hips.
Squeeze your outer glute at the top.
Lower under control. Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Place a hand on your top hip to check for unwanted rolling.
Keep the movement small and controlled rather than forcing the knee high.
Rest your head on your lower arm to keep your spine neutral.

name: Clamshell Hold
desc: The top position of the clamshell held for time: lying on one side with the knees bent and stacked, the upper knee lifted and the pelvis square, so the glute medius works isometrically instead of through repetitions.
steps: Lie on one side with the hips and knees bent about 45 and 90 degrees, heels together and knees stacked.
Stack the shoulders and hips vertically and brace the trunk so the pelvis cannot roll backwards.
Open the upper knee as far as it goes without the pelvis rotating, keeping the heels touching.
Hold that open position for the prescribed time, breathing normally.
Lower the knee under control and repeat on the other side.
tips: Stop the lift where the pelvis starts to roll back; the range is smaller than most people expect.
Keep the heels pressed together so the movement stays in the hip rather than the ankle.
Add a loop band above the knees only once the pelvis stays perfectly still.

name: Clap Push-Ups
desc: An explosive plyometric push-up developing chest power and fast-twitch muscle fibers.
steps: Begin in a standard push-up position.
Lower your chest to the floor.
Explosively push up so hands leave the ground.
Clap your hands together and land softly, returning to start.
Repeat.
tips: Land with soft elbows to absorb impact.
Ensure you have enough upper body strength before attempting.

name: Clean
desc: An Olympic lift pulling a barbell explosively from the floor to the front-rack position on the shoulders.
steps: Stand over a loaded barbell with feet hip-width apart.
Grip the bar just outside your knees with an overhand grip.
Drive explosively through your legs and extend your hips.
Pull yourself under the bar and catch it on your front deltoids.
Stand fully upright to complete the lift.
tips: Keep the bar close to your body as it travels up.
Finish your leg drive fully before pulling under the bar.
Catch with your elbows high so the bar rests on your shoulders.

name: Clean and Jerk
desc: A two-part Olympic lift cleaning a barbell to the shoulders, then driving it overhead in a split stance.
steps: Pull a loaded barbell from the floor to your shoulders as in a clean.
Stand fully with the bar racked on your front delts.
Dip slightly and drive the bar overhead explosively.
Split your legs to receive the bar with arms locked out.
Recover by stepping your feet back together.
tips: Stand fully and reset your position before starting the jerk.
Drive the bar up with your legs, not just your arms.
Lock your arms out as your feet land in the split.

name: Close-Grip Barbell Curl
desc: A standing barbell curl with a narrow grip, biasing the long head of the biceps and the brachialis.
steps: Stand holding a barbell with an underhand grip, hands closer than shoulder-width apart.
Start with the bar at the thighs, arms extended, elbows tucked to the sides.
Curl the bar up to the shoulders by flexing the elbows.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower under control.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the elbows pinned to the sides — do not let them drift forward.
If the narrow grip bothers your wrists, use an EZ-bar.

name: Close-Grip Dumbbell Bench Press
desc: A dumbbell bench press with dumbbells held together to increase triceps involvement.
steps: Lie on a flat bench and hold two dumbbells together over your chest.
Lower them to your chest keeping elbows close.
Press back up.
Repeat.
tips: Press the dumbbells together throughout the movement.
Keep elbows tucked.

name: Close-Grip EZ-Bar Bench Press
desc: A triceps-focused press using an EZ-bar with a narrow grip for wrist comfort.
steps: Lie on a flat bench and grip the inner curves of the EZ-bar.
Lower the bar to your chest with elbows tucked.
Press back up to full extension.
Repeat.
tips: The EZ-bar reduces wrist discomfort.
Keep the movement controlled.

name: Close-Grip EZ-Bar Curl
desc: An EZ-bar biceps curl with hands close together, biasing the long head of the biceps.
steps: Stand holding an EZ-bar with hands on the inner bends, palms up.
Keep the elbows tucked at the sides.
Curl the bar up to shoulder level, squeezing the biceps.
Lower under control to a full stretch.
Repeat for the prescribed reps.
tips: Keep the elbows pinned — do not let them flare forward.
Squeeze hard at the top.
Avoid swinging the torso for momentum.

name: Close-Grip Incline Bench Press
desc: An incline bench press with a close grip targeting the triceps and upper chest.
steps: Set bench to an incline. Grip the barbell with hands shoulder-width or closer.
Lower the bar to your upper chest.
Press back up.
Repeat.
tips: The incline increases the stretch on the long head of the triceps.
Tuck elbows to keep the focus on triceps.

name: Close Grip Lat Pulldown
desc: A lat pulldown variation using a close, parallel-grip handle to emphasize the lower lats and biceps.
steps: Sit at a lat pulldown machine and secure your thighs under the pad.
Grip the close-grip handle with palms facing each other.
Pull the handle down to your upper chest.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom.
Return under control and repeat.
tips: Lean back only slightly, not excessively.
Avoid using momentum to pull the handle down.
Drive your elbows down and back, not just your hands.

name: Close-Grip Pull-Ups
desc: A pull-up with a narrow overhand grip that increases biceps and inner-back activation.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with hands shoulder-width or narrower, palms away.
Pull yourself up until chin clears the bar.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: The narrow grip increases biceps involvement.
Avoid kipping for strength development.

name: Close Grip Push Ups
desc: A push-up variation with hands placed close together to emphasize the triceps.
steps: Assume a push-up position with hands directly under your shoulders.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your ribs.
Lower your chest toward the floor.
Press back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your elbows tracking backward, not flared out.
Maintain a rigid plank position throughout.
Slow the descent for greater triceps activation.

name: Close-Stance Leg Press
desc: A leg press with the feet set close together, increasing knee flexion and keeping the quadriceps prominent while the back remains supported against the pad.
steps: Set the seat and back pad so your lower back stays supported throughout the repetition.
Place your feet close together near the middle of the platform, with the toes and knees pointing along the same line.
Lower the sled by bending the knees and hips while keeping both feet flat and the knees tracking over the toes.
Press the platform away through the whole foot until the legs are extended without snapping the knees straight.
Return under control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use only as narrow a stance as lets the knees track comfortably over the toes.
Keep the heels down and avoid letting the knees collapse inward as the sled descends.
Do not trade pelvic position for depth; stop before the lower back starts to round off the pad.

name: Cobra Stretch
desc: A prone backbend that stretches the abdominals and front of the torso by lifting the chest.
steps: Lie face down with your hands under your shoulders.
Press through your hands to lift your chest off the floor.
Keep your hips and legs on the floor, shoulders relaxed.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Keep your elbows slightly bent — do not force full extension.
Draw your shoulders down away from your ears.

name: Cocoons
desc: A dynamic ab exercise combining a knee tuck and an upper-body crunch from a full-body extended position.
steps: Lie face-up on the floor with arms extended overhead and legs extended, hovering slightly off the floor.
Simultaneously tuck the knees toward the chest and sweep the arms forward into a crunch.
Try to touch the hands to the shins at the top.
Reverse the motion smoothly, re-extending arms and legs back to the hover.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Feet and hands never touch the floor between reps — that's the whole drill.
Exhale sharply at the top of the tuck.

name: Commando Pull-Up
desc: A pull-up variation done with a staggered grip: the hands sit one in front of the other on the bar and the body is turned sideways, so the head passes beside the bar on each repetition. It demands more from the lats, arms and trunk than a standard pull-up.
steps: Grip the bar with the hands one in front of the other, palms facing each other, and hang with the arms straight and the body turned sideways.
Brace the trunk and pull the shoulder blades down to start the movement.
Pull yourself up, driving the elbows down, until your head clears the bar on one side of it.
Pause briefly at the top with the chest close to the bar.
Lower under control to a full hang.
Take the head to the other side of the bar on the next repetition, or swap the hand positions each set.
tips: Keep the legs and trunk still; swinging turns the pull into a kip.
Alternate the sides evenly so both arms and lats do the same work.
Start with a few repetitions per set: the staggered grip is harder than a regular pull-up.

name: Concentration Curl
desc: An isolation curl performed seated for peak bicep contraction.
steps: Sit on a bench with legs spread, holding a dumbbell in one hand.
Brace your elbow against the inside of your thigh.
Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder.
Lower with control.
Repeat on both sides.
tips: Keep your upper arm vertical and let only the forearm move.
Avoid swinging your torso to help the weight up.
Match the reps on each arm to avoid muscle imbalances.

name: Copenhagen Plank
desc: A demanding side plank in which the top leg rests on a flat bench and the lower leg is held off the floor. The inner thigh muscles of the top leg and the obliques hold the body in a straight line, which makes it a classic exercise for the adductors and the trunk.
steps: Lie on your side next to a flat bench and place your top leg on it, with the inside of the foot or the lower part of the leg resting on the bench.
Prop yourself up on the elbow of your lower arm, directly under your shoulder.
Lift your hips so that your body forms a straight line from your head to your top foot, and let the lower leg hang or lift it toward the bench.
Keep your hips high and your trunk steady, and breathe evenly.
Hold for the planned time, then lower your hips back to the floor.
Rest, then switch sides.
tips: Start with the top knee on the bench and a short lever; move the foot of the top leg onto the bench only when the hold feels easy.
Press your forearm into the floor and keep your shoulder away from your ear.
Stop if you feel a sharp pull in the groin; the adductors need a gentle build-up.

name: Copenhagen Plank Raises
desc: A dynamic version of the Copenhagen plank: you hold a side plank with the top leg resting on a flat bench and lift the lower leg up to meet it, then lower it again. The inner thigh muscles of both legs and the obliques work together, and the movement is demanding for the adductors.
steps: Lie on your side next to a flat bench and place your top leg on it, with the knee or the inner foot resting on the bench.
Prop yourself up on the elbow of your lower arm, directly under the shoulder.
Lift your hips so that your body forms a straight line from your head to your top foot, with the lower leg hanging underneath.
Raise the lower leg up toward the bench until it nearly touches the top leg, keeping your hips high.
Lower the lower leg slowly without letting your hips drop, and repeat for the planned repetitions.
Rest, then switch sides.
tips: Start with the top knee on the bench and a short lever; move the foot of the top leg onto the bench only when the raises feel easy.
Keep your hips high and your body in one line; dropping the hips takes the load off the inner thighs.
Move slowly and stop if you feel a sharp pull in the groin; the adductors need a gentle build-up.

name: Cossack Squat
desc: A wide-stance lateral squat that sinks the body deep over one bent leg while the other stays straight, training single-leg strength, hip mobility, and adductor flexibility.
steps: Stand in a wide stance with toes turned slightly out.
Shift your weight to one side, bending that knee and sinking into a deep squat.
Keep the trailing leg straight with the heel down and toes up.
Sink as low as your mobility allows, keeping the chest tall.
Drive through the bent leg back to center, then repeat to the other side.
tips: Keep the working heel planted -- do not roll onto the toes.
Point the straight leg's toes up to keep tension in the adductors.
Hold a light weight at your chest for a counterbalance if needed.

name: Cow Face Pose
desc: A seated pose with the knees stacked and the arms clasped behind the back, stretching the outer hips on one side and the shoulders in opposite directions.
steps: Sit on the floor and cross one knee directly over the other so the knees stack in the midline.
Walk the feet out towards the hips and settle both sit bones evenly on the floor.
Reach the arm on the top-knee side up and bend it behind the head, then reach the other arm up the back to clasp.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, keeping the chest open and the spine tall.
Release and repeat with the other leg and arm on top.
tips: Sit on a folded blanket if one sit bone lifts off the floor.
Hold a strap between the hands when the fingers do not meet; forcing the clasp rounds the back.
Keep the top elbow pointing up rather than letting it drift out to the side.

name: Crab Dips
desc: A floor triceps exercise from the reverse tabletop position: with the hands behind the hips and the trunk lifted, the elbows bend and straighten to move the body up and down.
steps: Sit with the knees bent, the feet flat and the hands on the floor behind you, fingers pointing towards the heels.
Press into the hands and feet and lift the hips until the trunk is roughly level with the knees.
Bend the elbows straight back to lower the hips towards the floor without sitting down.
Push back up until the arms are straight, keeping the hips lifted.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions and lower the hips to finish.
tips: Keep the elbows pointing back, not flaring out to the sides.
Hold the hips high the whole set; letting them drop turns it into a rest.
Walk the feet further away for a longer lever and more triceps work.

name: Crescent Lunge
desc: A split-stance hold with the back heel lifted and the arms overhead, loading the front leg while the back hip stays long.
steps: Step one foot forward into a long stance with the back heel lifted and the toes pointing forward.
Bend the front knee to about ninety degrees so it stacks over the ankle.
Draw the back hip forward so both hip points face the front of the mat, then raise the arms overhead.
Hold the position for the prescribed time with the ribs down and the back leg straight.
Step the feet together and repeat on the other side.
tips: Widen the stance sideways a little if balance is the limiting factor.
Press the back heel towards the wall behind you to keep the rear leg working.
Lower the arms to the hips if reaching overhead pulls the lower back into an arch.

name: Cross-Body Crunch
desc: A floor oblique crunch that draws the opposite elbow and knee toward each other, hitting the obliques and rectus together.
steps: Lie face-up on the floor with knees bent and hands lightly behind the ears.
Crunch up and rotate, bringing the right elbow toward the left knee as the knee draws up.
Return to the starting position under control.
Repeat on the other side, alternating every rep.
tips: Twist from the ribcage, not the arms; the elbows follow the shoulders.
Lower back stays on the floor throughout.

name: Cross Body Hammer Curl
desc: A neutral-grip curl bringing the dumbbell across the body toward the opposite shoulder, emphasizing the brachialis and forearms.
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip.
Curl one dumbbell up across your body toward the opposite shoulder.
Keep your elbow stationary at your side.
Lower under control and repeat on the other side.
Continue alternating for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your elbow pinned at your side throughout the curl.
Avoid swinging your torso to lift the weight.
Lower under control rather than letting the dumbbell drop.

name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
desc: A standing stretch that targets the rear shoulder by drawing one arm horizontally across the chest.
steps: Stand tall and bring one straight arm across your chest.
Hook your other forearm under it.
Gently pull the arm closer to your chest.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep the stretching shoulder down, not shrugged.
Do not pull on the elbow joint itself.

name: Crow Pose
desc: An arm balance with the knees resting on the backs of the upper arms and the feet lifted, held by the shoulders, arms and trunk.
steps: Squat with the feet close together and place the palms shoulder-width apart on the floor in front of you.
Bend the elbows straight back and set the knees high onto the backs of the upper arms.
Shift the weight forward onto the hands until the feet float off the floor.
Hold the balance for the prescribed time, rounding the upper back and looking slightly forward.
Lower the feet under control.
tips: Look at the floor ahead of the hands, not back at the feet; the gaze drives the balance.
Place a cushion in front of you while you are learning to fall forward safely.
Grip the floor with the fingertips to stop the weight rolling into the wrists.

name: Crunches
desc: A basic abdominal exercise focusing on the rectus abdominis.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and hands behind your head.
Curl your upper body toward your knees, lifting your shoulder blades off the floor.
Squeeze your abs at the top.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
tips: Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands.
Exhale as you curl up and inhale on the way down.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor throughout.

name: Cycling
desc: Riding a road bicycle, used as steady endurance cardio. Seated on the saddle with your hands on the handlebars, you pedal in smooth circles; the thighs drive each pedal stroke, while the glutes, hamstrings and calves complete it.
steps: Adjust the saddle so your knee is only slightly bent when the pedal is at the bottom of the stroke.
Sit on the saddle with your hands on the handlebars, elbows slightly bent and shoulders relaxed.
Place the balls of your feet over the pedal axles.
Push each pedal down and forward, then let it come up and over the top in a smooth circle.
Keep a steady cadence and choose a gear that lets you pedal without bouncing on the saddle.
Ride for the planned time or distance, easing the pace for the last few minutes to cool down.
tips: Keep your knees tracking in line with your feet; knees that fall in or out usually mean the saddle or cleats need adjusting.
A higher cadence in an easier gear is kinder to the knees than grinding a hard gear slowly.
Keep your upper body relaxed and your back long rather than rounded or rocking from side to side.

name: Dancer Pose
desc: A standing balance on one leg where the free foot is held behind the body and pressed away, combining a backbend with a single-leg hold.
steps: Stand tall and shift the weight onto one foot, keeping that knee soft.
Bend the other knee and take hold of the inside of that ankle behind you.
Press the lifted foot back into the hand and reach the opposite arm forward as the chest lifts.
Hold the shape for the prescribed time with the standing hip level and the gaze steady.
Release the foot and repeat on the other side.
tips: Fix the eyes on one point ahead; a moving gaze is what usually breaks the balance.
Keep the lifted knee in line with the hip rather than letting it swing out sideways.
Use a strap around the lifted foot if the shoulder does not allow the direct grip.

name: Dumbbell Fly
desc: An isolation exercise that stretches and contracts the pectorals through a wide arc of motion.
steps: Lie flat on a bench with dumbbells held above your chest, palms facing each other.
With a slight bend in the elbows, lower the dumbbells out to the sides.
Return to the start by squeezing your chest.
Repeat.
tips: Keep a consistent bend in the elbows throughout.
Do not let the dumbbells go too low.

name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
desc: A beginner-friendly squat with one dumbbell held upright against the chest. The weight in front of you counterbalances your body, so it is easy to sit deep with an upright torso while the quadriceps and glutes do the work.
steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width and your toes turned out a little.
Hold one dumbbell vertically at your chest, with both hands cupped under the top end and your elbows pointing down.
Brace your trunk and sit your hips back and down, keeping your chest tall and the dumbbell close to your body.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, with your knees tracking over your toes and your heels flat.
Pause briefly in the bottom position, then drive through your whole foot to stand back up.
Repeat for the planned repetitions without letting the dumbbell drift away from your chest.
tips: Keep your elbows inside your knees at the bottom; they can lightly press the knees out and help you sit deeper.
Let the dumbbell stay at the chest rather than sinking toward your stomach, or your back will round to compensate.
If your heels lift, raise them on a small plate or turn your toes out a little more until you can stay flat.

name: Dumbbell Kickstand Deadlift
desc: A staggered-stance hip hinge with one dumbbell that loads the front leg while the back foot provides light balance support.
steps: Stand tall and step one foot back so only the toes lightly touch the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand at hip height.
Hinge at the hips, lowering the dumbbell toward mid-shin while keeping the back flat.
Keep most of your weight on the front foot throughout.
Drive through the front heel to return to standing. Complete all reps, then switch sides.
tips: Keep the dumbbell close to the shin on the descent.
Stop when you feel a stretch in the front hamstring.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.

name: Dumbbell Lunge
desc: A unilateral lower-body exercise with dumbbells targeting quads and glutes through a stepping motion.
steps: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides.
Step forward with one foot and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Push off the front foot to return.
Alternate legs.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your torso upright.
Front knee should track over your toes.

name: Dumbbell Overhead Carry
desc: A loaded walk with a single dumbbell locked out overhead, demanding shoulder stability and an upright trunk over every step.
steps: Clean or press a dumbbell to a locked-out position directly above your shoulder.
Push the arm all the way up so the elbow is straight and the biceps is close to your ear.
Brace your ribs down rather than letting your lower back arch to hold the weight up.
Walk forward with controlled strides, keeping the dumbbell stacked over your shoulder and hip.
Keep your eyes forward — tipping your head back to watch the weight drags your posture with it.
Carry for the desired distance, lower under control, then repeat with the other arm.
tips: Match the distance on both arms so the asymmetric load does not become an asymmetric adaptation.
A locked elbow is not optional. A soft elbow puts the whole load on the muscle instead of the skeleton and the set ends early.
If your ribs flare and your back arches, the weight is too heavy for your current overhead position — fix the position before adding load.

name: Dumbbell Preacher Curl
desc: A biceps isolation curl performed with a dumbbell in each hand and the upper arms supported on a preacher bench. The pad locks the elbows in place, so the biceps do the work with almost no swing.
steps: Adjust the seat so the armpits rest against the top of the pad and the upper arms lie flat along it.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip and let the arms hang down along the pad.
Curl both dumbbells up toward the shoulders without lifting the elbows off the pad.
Squeeze the biceps briefly at the top.
Lower the dumbbells slowly until the arms are almost fully extended, then repeat.
tips: Stop just short of full extension at the bottom to keep tension on the biceps and protect the elbows.
Keep the chest against the pad; leaning back lets the shoulders take over.
Lower the weights slowly; do not let them drop.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
desc: A compound movement targeting the lats and chest with a stretching motion.
steps: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell held above your chest, arms extended.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head in an arc, keeping slight bend in elbows.
Stretch until you feel tension in your lats and chest.
Pull the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Cup one end of the dumbbell with both hands for a secure grip.
Avoid excessive arching in your lower back during the stretch.
Lower only as far as your shoulder mobility comfortably allows.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Curl
desc: A curl variation with a pronated grip targeting the brachialis and forearm extensors.
steps: Hold dumbbells with an overhand grip at your sides.
Curl them up to shoulder height.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep wrists neutral throughout.
Controlled movement is key.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Wrist Curl
desc: A dumbbell wrist curl with palms down, training the forearm extensors.
steps: Sit on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, forearms resting on your thighs, palms down.
Let both wrists drop, lowering the dumbbells toward the floor.
Lift the backs of your hands toward the ceiling by extending your wrists.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Use a much lighter load than for a regular wrist curl.
Move only at the wrist.
Squeeze the back of the forearm at the top.

name: Dumbbell Shrug
desc: A dumbbell shrug targeting the upper trapezius for neck and upper back thickness.
steps: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides.
Shrug your shoulders straight up as high as possible.
Hold briefly, then lower.
Repeat.
tips: Do not roll your shoulders.
Focus on squeezing the traps at the top.

name: Dumbbell Skull Crusher
desc: A lying triceps extension with dumbbells allowing independent arm movement.
steps: Lie on a flat bench holding dumbbells over your chest.
Lower the dumbbells toward the sides of your head.
Extend your arms back up.
Repeat.
tips: Keep elbows pointing toward the ceiling.
Use a controlled tempo.

name: Dumbbell Somersault Squat
desc: A single-arm reaching squat with a dumbbell that adds rotation and shoulder mobility to a squat pattern.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width holding a dumbbell in one hand at the shoulder.
Squat down while reaching the dumbbell forward and across the body.
Reach the bottom of the squat with the dumbbell extended past the opposite knee.
Drive through the heels to stand up, returning the dumbbell to the shoulder.
Complete reps per side, then switch.
tips: Move slowly through the rotation to keep the spine controlled.
Use a light dumbbell — the long lever taxes the shoulder.
Push the knees out to keep the squat track stable.

name: Dumbbell Squat
desc: A squat loaded with a dumbbell in each hand at the sides, accessible without a barbell.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width, a dumbbell in each hand at the sides.
Brace the core and keep the chest up.
Squat down by hinging at the hips and bending the knees.
Descend until the thighs are parallel or below.
Drive through the heels to stand back up.
tips: Keep the chest up and the back flat throughout.
Push the knees out in line with the toes.
Use straps if grip becomes the limiting factor.

name: Dumbbell Step-Up to Balance
desc: A loaded version of the step-up to balance: holding a dumbbell in each hand, you step onto a low platform, drive the free knee up in front of you and stand tall on the working leg before stepping back down. The quadriceps and glutes lift the body and the weights while the hips and ankle keep you steady.
steps: Stand facing a low, stable step or bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging at your sides.
Place one foot flat on top of the step.
Press through the whole of the front foot and straighten that leg to lift your body onto the step.
As you rise, drive the other knee up in front of you until the thigh is about hip height.
Stand tall on the working leg and hold the knee-up position for a moment without leaning back.
Lower the free foot back to the floor under control, then step the working leg down as well and repeat; switch legs after the planned repetitions.
tips: Keep the weights hanging at your sides and still; swinging them or pulling them up with your arms takes the work away from the legs.
Keep your trunk upright and your hips level during the balance hold rather than tilting toward the lifted knee.
Start with light weights and a low step; add load only when you can hold the balance position without wobbling.

name: Dumbbell Sumo Squat
desc: A wide-stance squat with dumbbells held at the sides, biasing the inner thighs and glutes.
steps: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes turned out about 30 degrees.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Brace the core and keep the chest up.
Bend at the hips and knees to sit straight down into a deep squat.
Drive through the heels to return to standing.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Track the knees over the toes — do not let them cave in.
Keep the torso as upright as the hip mobility allows.
Choose lighter dumbbells than for a regular squat; grip is the limiter.

name: Dumbbell Svend Press
desc: A standing chest exercise pressing two dumbbells together in front of the body, where the inward squeeze keeps the pecs under constant tension.
steps: Stand and press two dumbbells together horizontally at chest height.
Maintain the inward squeeze on the dumbbells throughout.
Press the dumbbells forward until your arms are almost straight.
Pull them back to the chest under control.
Repeat for the prescribed reps.
tips: The squeeze on the dumbbells is what makes the exercise — do not let them separate.
Use a light load — pec activation is the goal, not load.
Keep the elbows slightly bent at the lockout.

name: Dead Bug
desc: A supine core exercise coordinating opposite limb extension to train deep core stability.
steps: Lie on your back with arms extended toward the ceiling and knees at 90 degrees.
Lower your right arm and left leg toward the floor while keeping the lower back pressed down.
Return to start.
Repeat on the other side.
Alternate.
tips: Press your lower back into the floor at all times.
Move slowly.

name: Dead Bug Hold
desc: The extended position of the dead bug held for time: lying on the back with one arm overhead and the opposite leg straightened just above the floor, keeping the lower back flat against the ground.
steps: Lie on your back with the arms pointing at the ceiling and the hips and knees bent to 90 degrees.
Press the lower back into the floor and keep it there for the whole set.
Extend one arm overhead and straighten the opposite leg until both hover just above the floor.
Hold that extended position for the prescribed time without letting the ribs flare or the back arch.
Return to the start and repeat with the other arm and leg.
tips: If the lower back lifts off the floor, keep the leg higher rather than reaching for the ground.
Breathe out slowly during the hold; holding your breath is what usually breaks the brace.
Keep the extended arm beside the ear, not out to the side.

name: Dead Hang
desc: A static hang from a pull-up bar with arms fully extended, primarily challenging grip and forearm strength.
steps: Grip a pull-up bar with palms facing away, shoulder-width apart.
Hang with your arms fully extended and feet off the ground.
Relax your shoulders and let your body hang.
Keep your core lightly engaged.
Hold for the desired duration.
tips: Build up your hold time gradually across sessions.
Breathe steadily throughout the hold instead of holding your breath.
Land softly with bent knees when you release the bar.

name: Decline Bench Press
desc: A compound chest press on a decline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, targeting the lower pectorals.
steps: Set the bench to a decline angle. Lie down and secure your feet.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand above your chest, then lower them to the sides of your lower chest.
Press the dumbbells back up to the start.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your back flat on the bench.
Use a spotter when working with heavier loads.

name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
desc: A barbell compound press on a decline bench emphasizing the lower chest.
steps: Set the bench to a decline angle. Lie down and secure your feet.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Lower the bar to your lower chest, then press back up.
Repeat.
tips: Control the descent.
Keep elbows at about 45 degrees to the torso.

name: Decline EZ-Bar Bench Press
desc: A decline press using an EZ-bar for a wrist-friendly grip targeting the lower chest.
steps: Set the bench to a decline. Secure your feet and grip the EZ-bar.
Lower the bar to your lower chest.
Press back up explosively.
Repeat.
tips: The angled grip reduces wrist strain.
Keep your core braced.

name: Decline Crunch
desc: A crunch performed on a decline bench, increasing the range of motion and resistance on the abs.
steps: Secure your feet at the top of a decline bench.
Lie back with hands crossed on your chest or behind your head.
Crunch up by flexing your spine toward your knees.
Squeeze your abs at the top.
Lower under control and repeat.
tips: Curl your spine up rather than pulling on your neck.
Exhale as you crunch and squeeze the abs at the top.
Lower slowly instead of dropping back to the bench.

name: Decline Dumbbell Fly
desc: An isolation fly movement performed on a decline bench to emphasize the lower chest.
steps: Lie on a decline bench holding dumbbells above your chest.
With a slight elbow bend, lower the dumbbells wide to each side.
Squeeze the chest to bring them back up.
Repeat.
tips: Do not fully lock out the elbows.
Focus on the stretch at the bottom.

name: Decline Push-Up
desc: A bodyweight push-up with feet elevated to increase upper chest and shoulder activation.
steps: Place your feet on an elevated surface and hands on the ground.
Lower your chest to the floor in a controlled manner.
Push back up to the start.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your body in a straight line.
The higher the elevation, the more upper chest is targeted.

name: Deep Squat Hold
desc: A static bottom-position squat held with the hips below the knees, the heels flat and the hands clasped in front of the chest. It builds endurance and mobility in the hips, knees and ankles.
steps: Stand with the feet slightly wider than the shoulders and the toes turned out.
Clasp the hands in front of the chest and sit the hips down between the heels.
Lower until the hips are below the knees while the heels stay flat on the floor.
Keep the chest up and press the elbows against the knees to push them out.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then stand up.
tips: Keep the heels flat; if they lift, place a small plate or wedge under them.
Push the knees out in line with the toes and keep the spine long.
Build the hold time gradually, standing to reset between sets.

name: Deficit Deadlift
desc: A deadlift performed standing on a low platform, extending the range of motion to build strength off the floor.
steps: Stand on a small platform with a loaded barbell over your midfoot.
Hinge down and grip the bar just outside your knees.
Drive through your legs to stand up while keeping the bar close.
Lock out your hips and knees at the top.
Lower under control and repeat.
tips: Keep your back flat; the extra depth makes rounding more likely.
Use less weight than your conventional deadlift to maintain positioning.
Take the slack out of the bar before initiating the pull.

name: Deficit Push Ups
desc: A push-up variation with hands on raised supports, lowering the chest below hand level for a greater range of motion.
steps: Place your hands on two elevated surfaces like parallettes or blocks.
Assume a plank position with hands under your shoulders.
Lower your chest below the level of your hands.
Press back up to extend your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Avoid letting your hips sag during the deep stretch.
Work within a pain-free depth and increase it gradually.
Keep your elbows tracking back rather than flaring wide.

name: Diamond Push Ups
desc: A close-hand push-up with thumbs and index fingers forming a diamond, shifting the emphasis onto the triceps.
steps: Assume a push-up position with hands close together forming a diamond.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Lower your chest toward your hands.
Press back up to extend your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your elbows tracking back along your sides, not flared out.
Hold your body in a rigid straight line from head to heels.
Lower with control until your chest reaches your hands.

name: Dolphin Pose
desc: An inverted V held on the forearms: the hips lift towards the ceiling while the shoulders take the load, which makes it the standard preparation for forearm inversions.
steps: Kneel and place the forearms on the floor shoulder-width apart with the elbows under the shoulders.
Tuck the toes and lift the hips up and back until the body forms an inverted V.
Press the forearms down and draw the shoulders away from the ears; let the heels stay high.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, keeping the neck relaxed between the arms.
Lower the knees to the floor to come out.
tips: Keep the elbows from sliding apart; a strap around the upper arms holds the width.
Bend the knees generously so the spine stays long instead of chasing straight legs.
Walk the feet slightly closer to the elbows to take more weight into the shoulders.

name: Donkey Calf Raise
desc: A bent-over calf raise that maximizes calf stretch by hinging at the hips.
steps: Bend at the hips and rest the forearms on a bench or sturdy support.
Place the balls of the feet on a raised platform with heels free.
Drop the heels below platform level for a full stretch.
Drive up onto the toes as high as possible, squeezing the calves.
Lower under control to a deep stretch.
tips: Pause briefly at the top to maximize the contraction.
Use a slow eccentric for full stretch.
Add a partner or weight on the lower back for resistance.

name: Doorway Chest Stretch
desc: An open-arm stretch that lengthens the chest and front shoulders by drawing the arms back.
steps: Stand tall and raise your arms into a goalpost position.
Bend your elbows ninety degrees, forearms vertical.
Draw your elbows back and squeeze your shoulder blades.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Keep your ribs down and avoid arching your back.
Stretch to mild tension, never to pain.

name: Double Dumbbell Kickstand Deadlift
desc: A staggered-stance hip hinge with two dumbbells that distributes load primarily through the front leg while the back foot lightly grounds for balance.
steps: Stand tall and step one foot back so only the toes touch the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at hip height.
Hinge at the hips, lowering both dumbbells toward mid-shin while keeping the back flat.
Keep most of your weight on the front foot throughout.
Drive through the front heel to return to standing. Switch sides after all reps.
tips: Keep the dumbbells close to the legs throughout the movement.
Stop when you feel a stretch in the front hamstring.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.

name: Double Dumbbell Overhead Carry
desc: A loaded walk with a dumbbell locked out above each shoulder, doubling the overhead load and removing the free arm that would otherwise help you balance.
steps: Clean or press a dumbbell to lockout above each shoulder.
Straighten both elbows fully and keep reaching up into the weights so the shoulders stay active, without letting the dumbbells sink down onto them.
Brace hard and keep your ribs down — with both arms overhead the temptation to arch is much stronger.
Walk forward with short, deliberate strides, keeping both dumbbells stacked over your shoulders.
Keep breathing shallowly and steadily instead of holding your breath for the whole carry.
Carry for the desired distance, then lower both weights under control.
tips: Start lighter than your single-arm carry weight per hand. Two arms overhead is not twice as easy, it is twice as much to stabilise.
Have a plan for bailing out before you start, and carry where you can drop the weights safely.
Short distances done well beat long ones done bent. Stop the set when your ribs start to flare, not when your shoulders give out.

name: Double Kettlebell Bicep Curl
desc: A standing biceps curl with one kettlebell in each hand, held by the handle. The offset mass at the bottom of the bell adds a mild grip and stability challenge.
steps: Stand holding a kettlebell in each hand by the handle, palms facing forward.
Keep the elbows tucked to the sides and the bells hanging at arm length.
Curl both kettlebells up toward the shoulders by flexing the elbows.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower under control to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Do not let the bells swing — control the eccentric.
Elbows stay pinned to the sides; no shoulder flexion.
Grip hard throughout; the bell wants to pull the wrist into extension.

name: Double Kettlebell Clean
desc: An explosive hip hinge that racks two kettlebells to the shoulders simultaneously, the foundation for double-KB pressing and jerking.
steps: Stand with two kettlebells on the floor between your feet, handles angled slightly inward.
Hinge at the hips, grip the handles, and hike the kettlebells back between the legs.
Explosively extend the hips to drive the kettlebells up along the body.
As they reach chest height, spear your hands through the handles to catch them at the rack position on the shoulders.
Lower back to the hang by hinging at the hips and guiding the bells between the legs.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Spear the hands through — don't let the kettlebells flip over and bang the wrists.
Drive with the hips; the arms only guide the path.

name: Double Kettlebell Clean and Press
desc: A full-body power exercise that cleans two kettlebells from the floor to the racked position at the shoulders and then presses both overhead to lockout in one continuous sequence.
steps: Stand with two kettlebells on the floor between your feet, feet about hip-width apart, and hinge at the hips to grip one handle in each hand.
Drive through your legs and extend your hips explosively to pull both kettlebells up, then rotate your elbows under and catch the bells in the racked position at the front of your shoulders.
Brace your core and press both kettlebells overhead until your arms are fully locked out.
Lower the kettlebells back to the racked position, then down to the floor under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep the kettlebells close to your body during the clean and punch your hands around and through the handles as you catch them, so the bells settle on your forearms instead of banging into them.
Use a slight dip-drive from the legs and hips to start the press, then finish with the shoulders — keep your core tight so you do not lean back under the load.
At lockout keep your wrists straight and the kettlebells stacked over your elbows and shoulders, with your head returning to a neutral position between the bells.

name: Double Kettlebell Dead Clean
desc: An explosive kettlebell movement cleaning two bells from the floor to the rack position, with each rep starting from a dead stop.
steps: Set two kettlebells on the floor between your feet.
Hinge down and grip both handles.
Drive explosively through your legs and hips.
Pull the kettlebells up and rotate them to the rack position.
Lower them back to the floor and repeat.
tips: Guide the bells close to your body as they travel up.
Keep your wrists straight as the bells settle into the rack.
Reset a tight hinge position before every rep.

name: Double Kettlebell Dead Split Snatch
desc: An Olympic-style kettlebell lift snatching two bells from the floor to overhead, caught in a split stance.
steps: Set two kettlebells on the floor between your feet.
Hinge down and grip both handles firmly.
Explosively pull the kettlebells overhead in one motion.
Drop into a split stance to catch them at lockout.
Recover by stepping feet back together.
tips: Punch up through the handles to achieve a stable overhead lockout.
Keep your front knee tracking over your foot in the split.
Stay tall through your torso as you drop under the bells.

name: Double Kettlebell Jerk
desc: An overhead lift using a double dip-drive to launch two kettlebells from the rack to lockout, the hallmark lift of kettlebell sport.
steps: Start with two kettlebells racked on the shoulders, elbows resting on the hips.
Perform a short dip at the knees, then explosively extend the legs to drive the kettlebells up.
As the bells rise, perform a second dip under them by bending the knees again.
Catch the kettlebells overhead with arms locked out, then stand fully upright.
Lower them back to the rack under control and repeat.
tips: The jerk is two dips, not one — the second dip is what lets you lock out with light arms.
Breathe on every rep, exhaling on each dip and drive, instead of holding your breath through the set.

name: Double Kettlebell Overhead Carry
desc: A loaded walk with a kettlebell locked out above each shoulder — the hardest of the carries to keep still, combining the offset mass of the bells with double the overhead load.
steps: Clean two kettlebells to the rack, then press or push press both to lockout overhead.
Straighten both elbows and settle each bell behind and above its wrist, with your wrists straight.
Pull your ribs down and brace hard before the first step; with both bells overhead there is nothing to counterbalance with.
Walk forward with short, controlled strides, keeping both bells stacked over your shoulders.
Keep looking straight ahead and breathe steadily through the carry.
Cover the desired distance, then lower both bells to the rack and down under control.
tips: Earn this one. Be comfortable with the single-bell overhead carry on both sides before loading two.
Only do it where you can safely drop both bells, and know which way you will step if you have to.
Distance should be short and posture perfect. The moment your back arches or a wrist folds, the set is finished.

name: Double Kettlebell Overhead Press
desc: A strict overhead press with two kettlebells from the rack position, demanding shoulder strength and a braced core.
steps: Clean two kettlebells to the rack position at your shoulders.
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Press both kettlebells straight overhead.
Lock out your arms at the top.
Lower back to the rack position and repeat.
tips: Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs before each press.
Keep your forearms vertical as you drive the bells up.
Avoid flaring your ribs or arching your lower back at lockout.

name: Double Kettlebell Push Press
desc: A push press with two kettlebells in the rack. The leg drive (single dip) lets you launch heavier loads overhead than a strict press — the middle tier between strict OHP and full jerk.
steps: Stand with two kettlebells racked at the shoulders, elbows down and tucked.
Feet shoulder-width, core braced.
Dip the knees slightly while keeping the torso vertical.
Explosively extend the legs and press both bells overhead in one motion.
Lock out with the bells over the mid-foot.
Lower back to the rack under control.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Only ONE dip — if you re-bend the knees under the bell, that is a jerk.
Drive from the legs, the arms finish.
The torso stays vertical throughout; no lean.

name: Double Kettlebell Rear Delt Row
desc: A bent-over row with a kettlebell in each hand and the elbows driven out wide of the torso, which shifts the work off the lats and onto the posterior deltoids and upper back.
steps: Stand a kettlebell just outside each foot with your feet about hip-width apart.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back until your torso is close to parallel with the floor, letting your knees bend slightly.
Take both handles with an overhand grip and let your arms hang straight down from your shoulders.
Row both bells up by driving your elbows out to the sides, away from your ribs rather than back along them.
Stop when your upper arms are roughly in line with your shoulders, and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower the bells under control until your arms hang straight again, and repeat for the desired reps.
tips: The wide elbow is the whole exercise. Let it drift in against your ribs and you are doing an ordinary double kettlebell row, training your lats instead of your rear delts.
Use less weight than you would for a normal row. The flared elbow is a long lever and the rear delts are a far smaller engine than the lats.
Hold the hinge angle steady. Standing up as you pull hands the work to the traps and lower back and shortens the range where the rear delts actually work.

name: Double Kettlebell Row
desc: A bent-over rowing exercise pulling two kettlebells to the hips, strengthening the lats and upper back.
steps: Hold a kettlebell in each hand and hinge forward at the hips.
Let your arms hang straight down from your shoulders.
Row both kettlebells to your hips by driving elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Lower under control and repeat.
tips: Hold your hinge angle steady; avoid standing up as you pull.
Keep your neck neutral by gazing at the floor ahead.
Brace your core to protect your lower back throughout.

name: Double Kettlebell Split Jerk
desc: An explosive overhead lift driving two kettlebells from the rack to lockout, caught in a split stance.
steps: Clean two kettlebells to the rack position at your shoulders.
Dip slightly by bending your knees.
Drive the kettlebells overhead explosively.
Split your legs to catch them with locked arms.
Recover by stepping feet back together.
tips: Keep your heels down during the dip to maintain power.
Time the split so your arms lock as your feet land.
Drive with your legs; your arms mainly guide the bells.

name: Double Kettlebell Swing Snatch
desc: A ballistic kettlebell exercise swinging two bells from between the legs to an overhead lockout in one motion.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding two kettlebells.
Hinge at the hips to swing the bells between your legs.
Explosively drive your hips forward to swing the bells up.
Punch through to catch both kettlebells overhead with locked arms.
Lower under control and repeat.
tips: Keep your arms relaxed and let your hips generate the power.
Let the bells roll smoothly around your wrists rather than flipping over.
Maintain a flat back during every backswing.

name: Downward-Facing Dog
desc: An inverted-V stretch that lengthens the hamstrings, calves, shoulders and back at once.
steps: Start on all fours with hands slightly ahead of your shoulders.
Tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back.
Straighten your legs and press your heels toward the floor.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Bend your knees if your lower back rounds.
Press the floor away to lengthen your spine.

name: Downward Dog Knee Tuck
desc: A moving core drill held in downward dog: the hips stay high while one knee is drawn in under the chest and sent back to the start, alternating sides. The shoulders support the whole set, so the trunk works without the low-hip position of a plank.
steps: Set up in downward dog with the hands shoulder-width apart and the hips high.
Press the floor away and brace the trunk so the lower back stays long.
Draw one knee in towards the chest, rounding the upper back slightly as it comes in.
Extend the leg back to the starting position under control.
Repeat with the other leg and keep alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the hips high; letting them drop turns this into a mountain climber.
Draw the knee in with the abdominals rather than by hopping off the standing foot.
Push the shoulders away from the ears so the upper body does not sink between the arms.

name: Downward Dog Pedal
desc: A warm-up performed in downward dog: the knees bend one at a time so each heel presses towards the floor in turn, taking the calf and the back of the ankle through a moving stretch instead of a static hold.
steps: Set up in downward dog with the hands shoulder-width apart and the hips high.
Bend one knee and let that heel lift while the opposite heel presses down towards the floor.
Switch sides smoothly, as if pedalling, keeping the hips high throughout.
Keep the hands pressing evenly so the shoulders stay stable.
Continue alternating for the desired number of repetitions or time.
tips: Keep the hips high; the point is the calves, not a deeper fold.
Press the whole hand into the floor so the wrists do not take all the load.
Move slowly enough to feel each side lengthen rather than bouncing.

name: Downward Dog to Knee Drive
desc: From three-legged dog the lifted leg folds forward so the knee travels towards the elbow or the nose, then extends back up. The shoulders hold the position while the trunk does the folding, one side at a time.
steps: Set up in downward dog and lift one leg behind you into three-legged dog.
Press both hands down and shift the weight slightly forward.
Round the upper back and drive that knee forward towards the elbow or the nose.
Extend the leg back up to three-legged dog under control.
Finish the repetitions on that side and repeat on the other.
tips: Let the upper back round as the knee comes in; a flat back stops the knee short.
Keep the shoulders over the wrists as you shift forward rather than collapsing past them.
Lift the leg only as high as the hips stay level on the way back out.

name: Downward Dog to Low Lunge
desc: The standard step-through: from downward dog one foot travels forward between the hands into a low lunge, then returns. It opens the hip flexor of the trailing leg and rehearses the transition used throughout flow practice.
steps: Start in downward dog with the hands shoulder-width apart.
Shift the weight forward and step one foot up between the hands.
Lower the back knee to the floor and sink the hips into a low lunge.
Press back through the hands, lift the back knee and step the front foot back to downward dog.
Repeat on the other side and keep alternating.
tips: Step the foot all the way to the hands rather than landing short and shuffling.
Pad the back knee with a folded mat if the floor is hard.
Keep the front knee above the ankle when the hips sink.

name: Downward Dog to Plank
desc: A moving transition between downward dog and a high plank: the hips travel from high to level and back, so the shoulders and trunk work through a full range instead of holding one position.
steps: Set up in downward dog with the hips high and the hands shoulder-width apart.
Shift the weight forward and lower the hips until the body forms a straight line in a high plank.
Hold the plank for a moment with the ribs down and the glutes engaged.
Press the floor away and lift the hips back up into downward dog.
Continue alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Move the hips, not the hands; the palms stay in the same place the whole set.
Keep the shoulders pushing away from the ears in both positions.
Slow the transition down if the lower back sags on the way into the plank.

name: Downward Dog to Upward Dog
desc: The vinyasa transition: the body travels from downward dog forward into upward dog and back, alternating between a shoulder-loaded inverted V and an open-chested backbend.
steps: Start in downward dog with the hips high and the hands shoulder-width apart.
Shift forward through plank and lower slightly, then press the chest through into upward dog with the thighs off the floor.
Draw the shoulders back and down and keep the neck long.
Tuck the toes, press the floor away and lift the hips back into downward dog.
Continue moving between the two positions for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Move the hips, not the hands; the palms stay planted the whole set.
Press the tops of the feet down in upward dog so the thighs actually lift.
Slow down through the middle of the transition rather than swinging between the ends.

name: Drag Curl
desc: A barbell curl where the elbows travel backward and the bar drags up the torso, eliminating front-delt assistance and emphasizing the long head of the biceps.
steps: Stand holding a barbell with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Start with the bar at the thighs and elbows at the sides.
Curl the bar by sliding (dragging) it straight up along your body.
As the bar rises, let the elbows travel backward so the bar stays in contact with your torso.
Stop when the bar reaches mid-chest; the biceps will be fully shortened.
Lower under control along the same path and repeat.
tips: Use significantly less weight than a standard curl — the altered mechanics make it much harder.
The bar should never move away from the body.

name: Dragon Flag
desc: A demanding core hold performed on a bench: gripping behind your head, you raise your entire body into a rigid straight line supported only by your upper back.
steps: Lie on a bench and grip it firmly behind your head.
Raise your body up so only your upper back stays on the bench.
Keep your body rigid in a straight line.
Lower your body under control until nearly horizontal.
Raise back up and repeat.
tips: Keep your body rigid from shoulders to toes and move only at the shoulders.
Lower as slowly as you can — the eccentric is the exercise.
Start with tucked or single-leg progressions before the full flag.

name: Dumbbell Bench Pull
desc: A prone rowing movement on a bench for strict upper back work.
steps: Lie face down on an incline bench holding dumbbells.
Let your arms hang straight down.
Pull the dumbbells up toward your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your chest glued to the bench throughout the pull.
Drive your elbows up and back rather than curling the weight.
Let your shoulder blades protract fully at the bottom for full range.

name: Dumbbell Calf Raise
desc: A weighted calf raise holding dumbbells at the sides, performed on an elevated edge for a full stretch.
steps: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Place the balls of your feet on a raised surface with heels hanging off.
Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
Squeeze your calves at the top of the movement.
Lower your heels below the platform to stretch the calves.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Avoid bouncing out of the bottom stretch position.
Keep your legs straight but not locked throughout.
Prevent your ankles from rolling outward as you rise.

name: Dumbbell Clean and Press
desc: A full-body power exercise in which two dumbbells are cleaned to the shoulders and then pressed overhead in one flowing sequence. It builds explosive hip power and strong shoulders and triceps.
steps: Stand with the feet hip-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand, hanging at your sides.
Hinge at the hips and bend the knees slightly to lower the dumbbells to just below the knees.
Explosively extend the hips and knees and shrug to pull the dumbbells up to the shoulders, catching them with the elbows forward.
Dip slightly at the knees and drive the dumbbells straight overhead until the arms are locked out.
Lower the dumbbells back to the shoulders, then to your sides, under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Let the legs and hips produce the power; the arms only guide the dumbbells.
Keep the dumbbells close to the body on the way up.
Finish each press with the ribs down and the glutes tight.

name: Dumbbell Curl and Press
desc: A standing compound movement that links a dumbbell curl to an overhead press: the weights are curled to the shoulders and then pressed straight overhead before being lowered. It works the biceps and shoulders in one smooth repetition.
steps: Stand tall with the feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with the palms facing forward.
Curl both dumbbells up to the shoulders, keeping the elbows close to the body.
Press the dumbbells overhead until the arms are fully extended.
Lower the dumbbells back to the shoulders under control.
Lower them to your sides with a controlled reverse curl, then repeat.
tips: Brace the abdominals and keep the ribs down so the press does not turn into a back bend.
Do not swing the weights up with the legs; use a load you can curl strictly.
Press in a slight arc so the dumbbells finish directly over the shoulders.

name: Dumbbell Deadlift
desc: A deadlift variation using dumbbells held in front of the thighs, training the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back.
steps: Stand with dumbbells in front of your thighs, feet hip-width apart.
Hinge at the hips and lower the dumbbells along your legs with a flat back.
Keep the dumbbells close to your shins throughout the descent.
Drive through your heels to return to standing.
Extend your hips fully at the top without hyperextending your lower back.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Brace your core before each rep to keep your spine stable.
Balance your weight over midfoot rather than your toes.
Keep your neck in line with your spine rather than looking up.

name: Dumbbell Face Pull
desc: A rear-delt and upper-back exercise performed by pulling dumbbells toward the face with a wide elbow path.
steps: Stand or sit holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended forward.
Bend your elbows and pull the dumbbells toward your face.
Flare your elbows out wide to shoulder height.
Squeeze your rear delts and upper back at the peak.
Lower the dumbbells back under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
Keep your upper arms roughly parallel to the floor.
Use a lighter weight to prioritize form over load.

name: Dumbbell Farmer's Walk
desc: This full-body exercise involves walking while holding heavy dumbbells, effectively building grip strength, core stability, and overall muscular endurance.
steps: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended at your sides.
Retract your shoulder blades and brace your core, maintaining a neutral spine.
Walk slowly and deliberately for a set distance or duration, taking short, controlled steps.
Keep your chest up and avoid leaning to one side as you walk.
Focus on maintaining a strong, stable posture throughout the movement.
tips: Use the heaviest dumbbells you can control without compromising form.
Breathe deeply and rhythmically to maintain core tension.
Imagine you are balancing a glass of water on your head.

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
desc: A dumbbell press performed lying on the floor, restricting the range of motion for joint-friendly pressing.
steps: Lie on the floor with a dumbbell in each hand at chest level.
Press the dumbbells upward until arms are extended.
Lower under control until elbows touch the floor.
Repeat.
tips: The floor limits shoulder strain at the bottom.
Keep wrists stacked over elbows.

name: Dumbbell Front Raise
desc: An isolation exercise targeting the anterior deltoid through a forward raise motion.
steps: Stand with dumbbells at your sides, palms facing your thighs.
Raise one or both dumbbells forward to shoulder height.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Avoid using momentum.
Slight elbow bend reduces joint stress.

name: Dumbbell Front Squat
desc: A squat holding dumbbells racked at the shoulders, keeping the torso upright and emphasizing the quads.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand resting on top of your shoulders.
Keep your elbows high and torso upright.
Lower your hips by bending knees until thighs are parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.
Maintain a neutral spine throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your elbows high so the dumbbells stay racked on your shoulders.
Sit down between your hips rather than folding forward.
Drive through the whole foot and keep your heels down.

name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
desc: The Dumbbell Hip Thrust is a highly effective compound exercise for building strong glutes and hamstrings, performed by thrusting the hips upwards with a dumbbell across the pelvis.
steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench, knees bent, feet flat, and a dumbbell across your hips.
Brace your core and drive through your heels, lifting your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes powerfully at the top of the movement, ensuring full hip extension.
Slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position with control, maintaining tension.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
