Extend your hips fully before pulling under the bar.
Lock your arms out and stabilize before standing up.

name: Sphinx Pose
desc: A gentle prone backbend on the forearms: the elbows stay under the shoulders and the chest lifts, so the lower back extends without any strain from the arms.
steps: Lie face down and place the forearms on the floor with the elbows directly under the shoulders.
Press the forearms and the tops of the feet down and lift the chest.
Draw the shoulders away from the ears and lengthen the back of the neck.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, breathing into the front of the chest.
Lower the chest to the floor and rest.
tips: Slide the elbows slightly forward for a gentler bend, back for a deeper one.
Keep the glutes soft so the lower back does not clench.
Stop where the position feels like a stretch, not like a pinch.

name: Spider Curl
desc: A curl lying face-down on an incline bench with arms hanging vertical, isolating the biceps through a strict range.
steps: Lie face down on an incline bench with arms hanging straight down.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip.
Keep your upper arms vertical as you curl the weights up.
Squeeze the biceps hard at the top.
Lower the dumbbells under control to full extension.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your chest glued to the pad for the whole set.
Squeeze at the top without letting the elbows drift backward.
Use the full range — the stretch at the bottom is half the value.

name: Spiderman Push-Up
desc: A push-up in which one knee is drawn up toward the elbow on the same side as the body lowers, like a spider climbing a wall. It trains the chest, shoulders and triceps while the obliques and hip flexors hold the trunk steady.
steps: Start in a high plank with the hands slightly wider than the shoulders and the body in a straight line.
Begin to lower the chest toward the floor and at the same time lift one foot off the floor.
Draw that knee out and up toward the elbow on the same side, keeping the hips low.
Press back up to the plank while returning the leg to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side and keep alternating.
tips: Keep the hips level; letting them pike or sag takes the work off the trunk.
Bring the knee toward the elbow without letting the foot touch the floor.
Lower with control and keep the elbows at about 45 degrees to the body.

name: Split Jerk
desc: An overhead lift driving the barbell up with a leg dip and receiving it in a split stance with locked arms.
steps: Hold the barbell across your front rack with elbows high.
Dip straight down by bending your knees slightly.
Explosively drive the bar overhead with your legs and arms.
Split your feet forward and back as the bar locks out.
Stand up by bringing your feet back together under the bar.
Lower the bar and repeat.
tips: Dip straight down rather than letting your torso tip forward.
Split your feet front and back as the bar locks out.
Bring your front foot back first when recovering.

name: Split Squat
desc: A stationary lunge lowering straight down in a split stance, building single-leg strength without a step.
steps: Stand in a split stance with one foot forward and one back.
Keep your torso upright and core braced.
Lower your hips straight down by bending both knees.
Stop when the back knee is just above the floor.
Drive through the front heel to return to the start.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Lower straight down rather than lunging forward.
Keep most of your weight over the front foot.
Keep the front heel planted throughout the rep.

name: Spoto Press
desc: A bench press variation pausing the bar just above the chest to build control and pressing power.
steps: Lie on a flat bench and grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulders.
Unrack the bar and hold it over your chest with arms extended.
Lower the bar until it is one inch above your chest.
Pause there for a full second without touching the chest.
Press the bar back up until your arms are extended.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your shoulder blades retracted and pinned to the bench.
Hold the bar motionless during the pause instead of letting it drift.
Use a lighter load than your standard bench press.

name: Squat Hold
desc: A static squat held with the thighs about parallel to the floor and the arms reaching forward for balance. It builds endurance in the quadriceps and glutes without equipment.
steps: Stand with the feet shoulder-width apart and the toes turned slightly out.
Reach the arms straight forward to counterbalance.
Squat down until the thighs are parallel to the floor, keeping the chest up and the heels down.
Hold the position, keeping the knees in line with the toes.
Stand up to finish.
tips: Keep the weight through the middle of the feet and the heels on the floor.
Do not let the knees cave in or the back round.
Build the hold time gradually and rest when the thighs begin to shake.

name: Squat Pulse
desc: A bodyweight squat variation in which you drop into the squat and then make short, controlled up-and-down pulses in the lower half of the movement without standing up. The constant tension keeps the thighs and glutes working through the whole set.
steps: Stand with the feet about shoulder-width apart and the toes turned slightly out, arms reaching forward for balance.
Squat down until the thighs are at least parallel to the floor, keeping the chest up and the heels down.
From the bottom, rise only a short way, a few inches, then sink back down.
Keep pulsing in the lower range without locking out or resting at the top.
Stand up fully when the set is finished.
tips: Keep the knees tracking over the toes; do not let them cave inward.
Stay in the bottom half of the squat; standing up between pulses removes the tension this move is for.
Keep the pulses small and quick but controlled; do not bounce off the bottom.

name: Stability Ball Hip Bridge
desc: A glute bridge with the feet on a stability ball, adding an anti-rotation and balance demand to the basic bridge pattern.
steps: Lie face-up on the floor and place both feet on top of a stability ball.
Arms rest at the sides on the floor for balance.
Squeeze the glutes and press the heels into the ball to raise the hips.
Finish with a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Lower the hips under control without the ball rolling away.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: The ball will try to drift — keep the feet pressed straight down.
No hyperextension at the top; stop when the body is in a line.

name: Stability Ball Knee Tuck
desc: A plank-position knee tuck with the feet on a stability ball, rolling the ball in under the hips to load the abs dynamically.
steps: Start in a high plank with both shins or the tops of the feet on top of a stability ball.
Hands are under the shoulders, body in a straight line.
Brace the core and pull the ball toward the chest by tucking the knees in.
Roll it back out by extending the legs fully back to the plank position.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Hips do not pike up; keep a level trunk throughout the roll-in.
Shoulders stay over the wrists — don't let them drift forward.

name: Stability Ball Push-Up
desc: A push-up performed with the feet on a stability ball, adding a strong anti-rotation demand to a standard push-up.
steps: Kneel in front of a stability ball and place your shins or feet on top of it.
Set the hands on the floor under the shoulders in a high-plank position.
Brace the core hard — the ball will want to roll sideways.
Lower the chest to the floor by bending the elbows.
Press back up to the starting position without letting the ball wobble.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Start with shins on the ball; feet-only is much harder.
If the ball drifts side to side, you're lacking core bracing — slow down.

name: Stability Ball Push-Up (Hands on Ball)
desc: An incline push-up performed with both hands on a stability ball and the feet on the floor. The unstable surface forces the chest, shoulders, and triceps to work harder while the core fights to keep the body rigid.
steps: Place both hands on top of a stability ball and walk your feet back into a straight-arm plank, body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and keep the ball steady beneath your hands.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the ball under control.
Press back up to full arm extension without letting the ball roll.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your body in a rigid straight line — do not let your hips sag or pike up.
Move slowly and deliberately; the wobble of the ball is what makes the exercise work, so resist it rather than fight it fast.
Set your hands slightly wider than shoulder width on the ball for a more stable base, and keep your elbows tucked to about 45 degrees.

name: Stability Ball Wall Squat
desc: A bodyweight squat with a stability ball pinned between the lower back and a wall, keeping the spine guided.
steps: Place a stability ball between your lower back and a wall.
Step the feet forward about a foot, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Squat down, letting the ball roll up the back as you descend.
Stop when thighs are parallel to the floor.
Drive through the heels to stand back up.
tips: Keep the weight in the heels and mid-foot.
Do not let the knees travel past the toes.
The ball should roll smoothly — do not lean off it.

name: Standing Adductor Stretch
desc: A standing stretch for the inner thigh: with your feet wide apart, you bend one knee and shift your weight to that side while the other leg stays straight. The straight leg's adductors lengthen as your hips sink toward the bent side.
steps: Stand with your feet about twice shoulder-width apart and your toes pointing forward.
Put your hands on the bent knee or in front of you for support.
Bend one knee and shift your hips sideways over that leg, keeping the other leg straight.
Keep your chest up and both feet flat on the floor.
Sink down until you feel a stretch along the inner thigh of the straight leg and hold it.
Shift to the other side and repeat.
tips: Keep the straight leg's foot flat or lift only the toes slightly; letting the foot roll out takes the stretch away.
Use your hands on the bent thigh to support your weight and keep your torso tall.
Do not bounce; sink slowly and stay within a stretch that feels strong but comfortable.

name: Standing Calf Stretch
desc: A staggered-stance stretch that lengthens the calf by pressing the rear heel down with the back leg straight.
steps: Step one foot back into a staggered stance.
Keep the back leg straight and the heel pressed down.
Bend the front knee and lean your weight forward.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep the rear heel flat and toes pointing forward.
Bend the rear knee slightly to target the lower calf.

name: Standing Forward Fold
desc: A standing stretch that lengthens the hamstrings and lower back by folding the torso over straight legs.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and legs straight.
Hinge at your hips and fold your torso down toward the floor.
Let your hands and head hang toward your feet.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Bend your knees slightly if your hamstrings feel tight.
Ease into the stretch slowly — never bounce.

name: Standing Forward Fold to Half Lift
desc: The familiar half-lift articulation: from a standing forward fold the chest lifts to a flat back with the spine long, then folds again. It teaches the difference between a rounded fold and a long-spine hinge.
steps: Stand with the feet hip-width apart and fold forward from the hips.
Rest the hands on the shins, the floor or blocks.
Slide the hands up the shins and lift the chest until the back is flat and the spine is long.
Fold back down, letting the head and neck release.
Continue alternating between the two for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a soft bend in the knees so the movement comes from the hips.
Lift to a flat back rather than looking up; the neck follows the spine.
Draw the shoulders away from the ears in the lifted position.

name: Standing Hip Abduction
desc: A bodyweight leg raise to the side while standing on the other leg. It trains the gluteus medius on the side of the lifted leg and, on the standing leg, the muscles that keep your hips level.
steps: Stand tall with your hands on your hips and your feet close together.
Shift your weight onto one leg and keep that knee slightly bent.
Lift the other leg straight out to the side, keeping the toes pointing forward and your trunk upright.
Raise the leg only as high as you can without leaning your upper body away from it.
Lower the leg slowly back next to the standing foot.
Complete the planned repetitions, then repeat on the other leg.
tips: Keep your hips square and your trunk still; leaning away from the lifted leg takes the work away from the hip.
Move with control on the way down as well; do not let the leg swing.
Hold on to a wall or a chair if you cannot stay balanced; add a loop band around your thighs once the movement is easy.

name: Standing Quad Stretch
desc: A standing balance stretch that lengthens the quadriceps by pulling the heel toward the glute.
steps: Stand on one leg, holding a wall for balance if needed.
Bend the other knee and grab that ankle behind you.
Pull the heel toward your glute, keeping knees together.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Tuck your pelvis under to deepen the stretch.
Keep your knees close together throughout.

name: Standing Side Bend
desc: A standing stretch that lengthens the obliques and lats by reaching overhead and bending to one side.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width and reach both arms overhead.
Clasp your hands and lengthen up tall.
Bend smoothly to one side in a long curve.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep both feet planted and hips steady.
Reach up and over rather than just leaning down.

name: Standing Side Bend Flow
desc: A standing lateral flow: the arms reach overhead and the trunk bends from side to side in a controlled rhythm, lengthening the side body without holding either end position.
steps: Stand with the feet hip-width apart and reach both arms overhead.
Bend the trunk to one side, keeping both feet planted and the hips level.
Return through the centre with the ribs stacked over the pelvis.
Bend to the other side in the same way.
Keep alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Bend sideways only: letting the chest rotate turns it into a twist.
Keep both heels down so the movement stays in the trunk.
Move with the breath rather than bouncing at the end of the range.

name: Standing Split
desc: A standing forward fold with one leg lifted behind: the torso folds over the standing leg while the free leg reaches towards the ceiling.
steps: From a forward fold, place both hands on the floor or on blocks beside the standing foot.
Shift the weight onto one leg and lift the other leg behind you.
Keep the standing leg straight and the hips as level as the lift allows.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, drawing the chest towards the standing shin.
Lower the lifted foot down and repeat on the other side.
tips: Level the hips first and accept a lower lift; an open hip turns this into a different pose.
Use blocks under the hands so the spine can stay long.
Hold the standing ankle with one hand only when the balance is already steady.

name: Step-Up to Balance
desc: A single-leg step-up that finishes with a balance hold: you step onto a low platform, drive the free knee up in front of you and stand tall on the working leg before stepping back down. The quadriceps and glutes lift the body while the hips and ankle work to keep you steady.
steps: Stand facing a low, stable step or bench and place one foot flat on top of it.
Press through the whole of the front foot and straighten that leg to lift your body onto the step.
As you rise, drive the other knee up in front of you until the thigh is about hip height.
Stand tall on the working leg and hold the knee-up position for a moment without leaning back.
Lower the free foot back to the floor under control, then step the working leg down as well.
Complete the planned repetitions on one leg, then switch to the other.
tips: Keep the whole foot on the step and push through it; pushing off the floor leg takes the work away from the front leg.
Keep the trunk upright and your hips level during the balance hold rather than tilting toward the lifted knee.
Choose a step low enough to stand up on without hopping; use a hand on a wall to start if balance is a limit.

name: Step Ups
desc: A lower-body exercise stepping onto a bench, building strength in the quads and glutes.
steps: Stand facing a sturdy box or bench.
Place one foot fully on the box surface.
Drive through that heel to lift your body onto the box.
Bring your trailing foot up to stand fully on the box.
Step back down leading with the same foot.
Alternate legs or complete all reps on one side before switching.
tips: Push through the lead heel rather than springing off the back leg.
Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward excessively.
Control the descent instead of dropping off the box.

name: Stiff Leg Deadlift
desc: A hip hinge with nearly straight legs, lowering the bar along the thighs to stretch and load the hamstrings.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell in front of your thighs.
Keep your legs nearly straight with only a slight knee bend.
Hinge at the hips and lower the bar along your legs.
Go as low as your hamstring flexibility allows with a flat back.
Drive through your heels to return upright.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Push your hips back and keep the bar close to your legs.
Go only as deep as a flat back allows.
Feel the hamstrings load in the stretch, then drive the hips forward to stand.

name: Straight-Bar Cable Front Raise
desc: A front raise on a low cable pulley with a straight bar attachment held in both hands. Unlike the one-armed cable front raise, both arms drive the same bar, and the cable keeps tension on the front delts through the whole range.
steps: Attach a straight bar to a low cable pulley and stand facing away from the machine with the cable running forward past your legs.
Hold the bar with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart, arms hanging straight down in front of your thighs.
Keep the elbows almost straight and the core braced so the torso does not lean back.
Raise the bar forward in a smooth arc until it reaches shoulder height.
Lower it under control back to the thighs and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a light weight — swinging the bar up with the legs or leaning back takes the work off the front delts.
Stop at shoulder height; raising the bar higher shifts the load onto the traps.
Keep the wrists neutral rather than letting them bend back under the bar.

name: Straight Bar Dips
desc: A dip performed on top of a single straight bar instead of parallel bars: from a straight-arm support over the bar, the body lowers until the chest nears the bar, then presses back up.
steps: Grip a straight bar overhand, slightly wider than shoulder-width, and jump into a straight-arm support on top of it with the bar at your hips.
Lean your chest slightly forward and bend your elbows to lower yourself toward the bar, keeping the elbows pointing back.
Stop when the bar is close to your upper chest or at the deepest point you can control.
Press down through the bar to straighten your arms and return to the support position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Lean the chest forward over the bar as you lower; the bar is in front of you, so staying upright tips you backwards.
Engage your core to keep your body from swinging.
This is a harder wrist and shoulder position than standard dips -- build up volume gradually.

name: Strict Curl
desc: A standing curl performed without any body English — the torso stays still and the elbows stay pinned, so the biceps do all the work.
steps: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides and palms facing forward.
Pin your elbows against your sides and brace your core so your torso cannot swing.
Curl both dumbbells up by bending only at the elbows.
Lower them under control until your arms are straight.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Standing with your back against a wall or post is a useful self-check — if your shoulders or hips leave it, you are using momentum.
Keep the elbows from drifting forward; the upper arms should stay vertical throughout.
Lower slower than you lift — the strict version lives in the descent.

name: Suitcase Carry
desc: A loaded walk with the weight in one hand only, so the trunk has to resist bending toward the load for the whole distance — the unilateral counterpart to the farmer's walk.
steps: Stand beside a single kettlebell or dumbbell with your feet under your hips.
Hinge at the hips, take the handle in one hand and stand up with the weight hanging at your side.
Pull that shoulder down and back, and brace as if you were about to be pushed sideways.
Walk forward with normal, even strides, keeping your torso upright and square rather than leaning away from the weight.
Keep the free arm relaxed at your side instead of sticking it out as a counterweight.
Carry for the desired distance or time, set the weight down under control, then repeat on the other side.
tips: Do the same distance on both sides. The whole value is in the asymmetry, and it only works if you load both directions equally.
If you find yourself tipping toward the weight or hiking the opposite hip, the weight is too heavy — this is a posture drill first.
Grip usually gives out before the trunk does. That is a legitimate training effect, but if it is always the limit, use straps for the heavier sets.

name: Sumo Deadlift
desc: A deadlift variation with a wide stance that shifts emphasis to the glutes, quads, and inner thighs.
steps: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes pointed outward.
Grip the bar between your legs.
Brace your core and drive through your heels to stand.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep the bar close to your body.
Push your knees out in line with your toes.

name: Sumo Squat
desc: A barbell squat performed with a wide stance and turned-out toes, emphasizing the glutes and quads.
steps: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width and toes turned out.
Hold a barbell across your upper back.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Bend at the hips and knees to lower into a deep squat.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Push your knees outward in line with your toes.
Keep the bar path vertical over the middle of your feet.
Avoid letting your lower back round at the bottom of the squat.

name: Superman
desc: A bodyweight lower-back exercise performed prone, lifting arms and legs simultaneously.
steps: Lie face down with arms extended overhead.
Simultaneously lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor.
Hold briefly at the top.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Squeeze glutes as you lift.
Avoid jerking movements.

name: Supine Spinal Twist
desc: A lying twist that stretches the lower back, glutes and obliques by dropping a bent knee across the body.
steps: Lie on your back and bend one knee toward your chest.
Guide that knee across your body toward the floor.
Stretch your arms out wide and turn your head away.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep both shoulders on the floor.
Relax and keep breathing throughout.

name: Supine Windshield Wipers
desc: A lying rotation drill: with the knees bent or the legs raised, both legs swing from side to side like wipers while the shoulders stay pinned to the floor.
steps: Lie on your back with the arms out to the sides and the knees bent over the hips.
Brace the trunk so the lower back does not lift off the floor.
Lower both legs together towards one side as far as the shoulders stay down.
Bring them back through the centre and lower to the other side.
Keep alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Both shoulders stay on the floor; the range is defined by them, not by the legs.
Keep the knees together so the pelvis moves as one unit.
Straighten the legs for a much harder version once the control is there.

name: Supported Shoulderstand
desc: An inversion resting on the shoulders and upper arms with the hands supporting the back, the body stacked vertically over the shoulders.
steps: Lie on your back, ideally with a folded blanket under the shoulders and the head off it.
Lift the legs overhead and support the lower back with both hands, elbows shoulder-width apart.
Walk the hands up the back and stack the hips over the shoulders until the body is vertical.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, keeping the head and neck completely still.
Lower the legs overhead and roll down slowly with the hands supporting the back.
tips: Keep the weight on the shoulders and upper arms, never on the neck.
Do not turn the head while inverted.
Build up with legs-up-the-wall and plow pose before holding this one for long.

name: Supported Single-Leg Stand
desc: A basic balance exercise in which you stand on one leg with a light hand on a chair or wall for support. The raised knee is held at hip height, and the standing leg keeps the ankle, knee and hip steady, which makes it a gentle starting point for balance work.
steps: Stand tall beside a sturdy chair, wall or rail and rest one hand lightly on it.
Shift your weight onto the leg nearer the support and keep that knee soft.
Lift the other knee in front of you until your thigh is about hip height.
Keep your chest tall, your hips level and your eyes on a fixed point ahead.
Hold the position for the planned time, using the support only as much as needed.
Lower the foot, rest briefly and repeat on the other leg.
tips: Press the standing foot evenly into the floor and let the toes spread; the ankle makes constant small adjustments.
Use only your fingertips on the support, and let go for a moment once you feel steady.
Do not lean toward the support or lift the hip; keep the pelvis level the whole time.

name: Svend Press
desc: A plate-squeeze press that loads the pecs through isometric adduction as you extend the weight away from the chest.
steps: Stand upright holding a single weight plate (or two pressed together) between your palms at chest height.
Squeeze the plates hard to generate tension through the pecs.
Press the plates straight out in front of you until the arms are fully extended.
Pause briefly, keeping the squeeze, then return the plates to the chest.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: The harder you squeeze the plates, the more chest activation you get.
Keep the plates at sternum height throughout — do not let them drop toward the hips.

name: Tandem Stance
desc: A balance hold in which one foot is placed directly in front of the other, heel touching toes, so your base of support is as narrow as a line. Holding the position with your arms out trains the ankles and hips to keep the body steady.
steps: Stand tall with your feet together and your arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Step one foot forward and place it directly in front of the other, heel against toes.
Spread your weight evenly over both feet and keep your knees soft.
Look at a fixed point ahead of you and keep your hips and shoulders level.
Hold the position for the planned time, using your arms to correct small sways.
Swap the front foot and repeat.
tips: Do this beside a counter or wall at first so you can reach out if you lose your balance.
Keep your gaze on a fixed point; looking down makes it harder.
Make it harder by closing your eyes or standing on a folded towel once you can hold it for 30 seconds.

name: Thoracic Bridge
desc: A mobility hold that lifts the hips from a seated, hands-behind position into a reverse tabletop and opens the chest, extending the thoracic spine while the glutes and shoulders hold the bridge.
steps: Sit on the floor with knees bent and hands behind you, fingers pointing back.
Press through your hands and feet to lift your hips off the floor.
Continue pressing until your chest opens and your arms are extended.
Drop your head back and hold the position.
Breathe steadily while maintaining the bridge.
Lower back down under control.
tips: Drive the hips high and squeeze the glutes to protect the lower back.
Keep the feet flat and the weight even between hands and feet.

name: Thread the Needle
desc: A kneeling rotation: one arm slides under the body and the shoulder and side of the head rest on the floor, rotating the thoracic spine passively.
steps: Start on all fours with the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
Slide one arm underneath the body, palm facing up, until the shoulder and the side of the head rest on the mat.
Keep the hips stacked over the knees and walk the top hand forward or wrap it behind the back.
Hold the twist for the prescribed time, breathing into the upper back.
Press the top hand into the floor to come up and repeat on the other side.
tips: Keep the hips high over the knees; dropping them turns the rotation into a side bend.
Rest the head on a block if the shoulder cannot reach the floor comfortably.
Let the shoulder settle with the breath instead of pushing the twist deeper by force.

name: Thread the Needle Flow
desc: The moving version of thread the needle: from all fours the arm threads under the body and then opens back up towards the ceiling, rotating the thoracic spine through its full range.
steps: Start on all fours with the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
Slide one arm under the body until the shoulder approaches the mat.
Reverse the motion and open that arm up towards the ceiling, following the hand with the eyes.
Return through the centre and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Change sides and repeat.
tips: Keep the hips over the knees so the rotation stays in the upper back.
Move at an even tempo instead of throwing the arm open.
Let the head follow the hand rather than leading the movement.

name: Three-Legged Downward Dog
desc: Downward dog with one leg lifted: the shoulders carry more load while the lifted leg extends in line with the spine and the hips stay square.
steps: Set up in downward dog with the hands shoulder-width apart and the hips high.
Press both hands evenly into the floor and shift the weight slightly forward.
Lift one leg behind you until it is in line with the spine, keeping both hip points level.
Hold the position for the prescribed time with the standing heel reaching down.
Lower the leg and repeat on the other side.
tips: Keep the lifted hip from opening; a square pelvis matters more than height.
Press the base of the index finger down so the wrists stay comfortable.
Bend the standing knee slightly if the hamstring limits the shape.

name: Thruster
desc: A full-body barbell movement combining a front squat with an overhead press in one fluid drive.
steps: Hold a barbell in a front rack position with elbows high.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down to parallel while keeping your torso upright.
Drive up out of the squat and press the bar overhead in one motion.
Lock out your arms at the top with the bar overhead.
Lower the bar back to the front rack and repeat.
tips: Use the momentum from the squat drive to launch the press.
Keep your elbows high so the bar rests on your shoulders, not your wrists.
Finish each rep with the bar locked out over your ears.

name: Toes to Bar
desc: An advanced hanging core exercise on a pull-up bar requiring hip flexion strength and lat engagement to touch the toes to the bar.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms fully extended and body still.
Engage your lats and core to prevent swinging.
Raise your legs with straight knees, reaching your toes up toward the bar.
Touch the bar with your toes, then lower your legs under control.
Repeat for the desired reps.
tips: Initiate the movement from your core, not by kicking with momentum.
Exhale forcefully as you raise your legs to increase intra-abdominal pressure.
If you cannot reach the bar yet, build up with hanging leg raises first; they are the easier step towards it.

name: Torso Twists
desc: A standing rotational warm-up that turns the rib cage from side to side while the pelvis stays comparatively stable, mobilising the thoracic spine and trunk.
steps: Stand with the feet about shoulder-width apart and the knees softly bent.
Brace lightly and hold the hands together in front of the chest.
Rotate the rib cage to one side without shifting the feet.
Return through centre and rotate to the other side.
Continue alternating smoothly through a comfortable range.
tips: Turn from the upper back rather than wrenching the lower spine.
Keep the hips mostly forward and distribute the weight evenly between the feet.
Use a controlled rhythm; this is mobility work, not a ballistic swing.

name: Treadmill Running
desc: A running cardio movement performed on a motorised belt, holding a chosen pace and distance indoors with the surface and gradient under your control.
steps: Step onto the treadmill with a foot on each side rail, start the belt at a walking speed and step on once it is moving.
Build up to your running pace, landing under your hips rather than reaching out in front of you.
Run tall with your shoulders relaxed, your elbows bent at about ninety degrees and your arms swinging forward and back, not across your body.
Keep your eyes forward and stay in the middle of the belt instead of drifting back toward the rear roller.
Hold the pace for the desired time or distance, then slow the belt and walk for a few minutes before stepping off.
tips: Clip the safety key to your waistband — it is the only thing that stops the belt if you lose your footing.
Do not hold the handrails while running. Leaning on them shortens your stride, twists your posture and hides how hard you are actually working.
A one to two percent incline makes indoor running feel closer to running outdoors, where you have to push through air resistance.

name: Tree Pose
desc: A one-legged standing balance with the sole of the free foot placed on the inner calf or thigh and the hips level.
steps: Stand tall and shift the weight onto one foot.
Place the sole of the other foot on the inner calf or the inner thigh, avoiding the knee.
Press the foot and the leg into each other and level the hips.
Bring the hands to the chest or overhead and hold for the prescribed time.
Lower the foot and repeat on the other side.
tips: Never rest the foot against the side of the knee; above or below it only.
Fix the gaze on a still point to steady the balance.
Keep the pelvis facing forward instead of letting the lifted knee pull it open.

name: Triangle Pose
desc: A wide-stance pose with both legs straight and the torso tilting sideways over the front leg, lengthening the hamstring and the whole side body.
steps: Stand wide with the front foot turned out and the back foot angled slightly in.
Keep both legs straight and reach the front hand forward as the hips shift back.
Tilt sideways and bring the bottom hand to the shin, a block or the floor, top arm reaching up.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, turning the chest towards the ceiling.
Press into the feet to come up and repeat on the other side.
tips: Reach out over the front leg before you tilt down; folding early collapses the pose.
Use a block under the bottom hand rather than dragging the chest towards the floor.
Keep both legs straight and the kneecaps lifted.

name: Dumbbell Tricep Kickback
desc: An isolation exercise for the triceps performed in a bent-over position.
steps: Hinge forward at the hips, holding a dumbbell with elbow bent at 90 degrees.
Extend your arm straight back, squeezing the tricep.
Hold briefly at full extension.
Lower with control.
Repeat on both sides.
tips: Keep your upper arm locked parallel to the floor throughout.
Use a light dumbbell and avoid swinging it with momentum.
Support your torso with your free hand on your thigh if needed.

name: Triceps Dip Hold on Dip Bars
desc: An isometric hold at the bottom of the parallel-bar dip: you lower yourself between the bars and stop with the elbows bent, leaning slightly forward. The triceps, the chest and the front of the shoulders stay under tension at the point where the dip is hardest.
steps: Grip the parallel bars of a dip station, press up and straighten your arms with your shoulders pushed down away from your ears.
Lean slightly forward, keep your legs together and cross your feet behind you if you want.
Lower yourself slowly by bending your elbows until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Stop there and hold, with your elbows pointing back and your chest open.
Keep your shoulders down and your body steady while you hold for the planned time.
Press back up to straight arms and step down.
tips: Do not sink so far that your shoulders roll forward; if they do, hold a little higher.
Keep the elbows close to your body to load the triceps; flaring them sends the work to the chest and the shoulders.
Use a bench or a pair of stable boxes under your feet if the hold is too hard at first.

name: Triceps Dip Hold on Bench
desc: An isometric hold at the bottom of the bench dip: with your hands on the edge of a bench behind you and your legs out in front, you lower your body and stop with the elbows bent. The triceps work hard at the point where the dip is hardest, with less load on the shoulders than a deep dip on bars.
steps: Sit on the edge of a bench, place your hands next to your hips with your fingers pointing forward and walk your feet out so that your legs are straight.
Slide your hips off the bench and straighten your arms to hold your weight.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until they reach about 90 degrees, keeping your back close to the bench.
Stop there and hold, with your elbows pointing straight back and your chest open.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears while you hold for the planned time.
Press up to straight arms and sit back down.
tips: Do not drop lower than 90 degrees at the elbow; going deeper puts a lot of stress on the front of the shoulders.
Keep your back close to the bench and your elbows pointing back, not out to the sides.
Bend your knees and bring your feet closer to make the hold easier.

name: TRX Bicep Curl
desc: This exercise uses a suspension trainer to isolate and strengthen the biceps brachii and brachialis muscles, building upper arm strength and hypertrophy.
steps: Adjust the suspension trainer straps to a medium length.
Stand facing the anchor point, grasp the handles with an underhand grip, and lean back until your arms are fully extended.
Keep your body straight and core engaged, pull your chest towards your hands by bending your elbows.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position, controlling the descent.
Maintain tension throughout the set.
tips: Adjust your body angle to increase or decrease difficulty; leaning further back makes it harder.
Keep your elbows high and fixed to isolate the biceps effectively.
Avoid swinging your body or using momentum; focus on a controlled contraction.
Ensure a full range of motion, from full extension to a strong peak contraction.

name: TRX Chest Press
desc: A compound push exercise using a suspension trainer to build chest strength and stability.
steps: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to mid-calf height.
Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding a handle in each hand, arms extended.
Lean forward into a plank position, keeping your body straight from head to heels.
Lower your chest towards your hands by bending your elbows, maintaining tension in the straps.
Press back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms and squeezing your chest.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the movement to maintain a rigid plank.
Control the eccentric (lowering) phase for better muscle activation.
Adjust your foot position to modify difficulty: closer to the anchor (more horizontal) is harder, further away (more upright) is easier.
Ensure your elbows track slightly out and back, not flaring wide.

name: TRX Face Pull
desc: The TRX Face Pull is a compound pulling exercise targeting the posterior deltoids and rhomboids, using a suspension trainer to improve upper back strength and posture.
steps: Grasp the TRX handles with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Lean back until your arms are fully extended and your body forms a straight line.
Pull the handles towards your face, driving your elbows high and wide.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the peak contraction.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control.
tips: Maintain a rigid torso throughout the movement; avoid arching your lower back.
Focus on initiating the pull with your upper back muscles, not just your arms.
Adjust your body angle to modify difficulty: a more horizontal position is harder.

name: TRX Hamstring Curl
desc: This isolation exercise uses a suspension trainer to target the hamstrings, glutes, and calves by curling the heels towards the glutes.
steps: Lie on your back with heels in the suspension trainer cradles, knees bent at 90 degrees.
Lift your hips off the floor, creating a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Extend your legs forward, maintaining hip elevation and core tension.
Pull your heels back towards your glutes, contracting your hamstrings forcefully.
Control the movement, avoiding any drop in hip height throughout the set.
tips: Keep your core braced to prevent your hips from sagging.
Focus on a strong hamstring contraction at the peak of the curl.
Control the eccentric phase by slowly extending your legs.

name: TRX Lunge
desc: A beginner-friendly unilateral lower body exercise using a suspension trainer to target the quadriceps and glutes, while also engaging the hamstrings and gluteus medius for stability.
steps: Stand facing away from the anchor point with the suspension trainer straps behind you, hands on your hips or free for balance.
Place the top of one foot in the foot cradles and extend that leg behind you.
Brace your core and lower your body by bending the front knee, keeping your torso upright.
Descend until your front thigh is parallel to the floor or just below, maintaining tension on the suspension trainer.
Drive through your front heel to return to the starting position, extending the front leg.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch legs and repeat per side.
tips: Keep your front knee tracking over your toes, avoiding inward collapse.
Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement, preventing excessive arching or rounding.
Control the eccentric (lowering) phase to maximize muscle engagement.
Adjust your distance from the anchor point to modify difficulty.

name: TRX Pistol Squat
desc: A challenging unilateral leg exercise using a suspension trainer to assist balance and depth, primarily targeting the quadriceps and glutes.
steps: Anchor the suspension trainer and hold the handles with both hands, arms extended.
Stand tall, lift one leg straight out in front of you, keeping it off the ground.
Initiate the squat by pushing your hips back and bending the standing knee, lowering your body as deep as possible.
Keep your chest up, back straight, and use the TRX for balance and support as needed.
Drive through your heel to return to the starting position, extending the standing leg fully.
Complete all reps on one side before switching to the other.
tips: Maintain tension on the TRX straps throughout the movement for stability.
Focus on controlled descent and powerful ascent.
Keep the non-working leg extended and elevated to engage the hip flexors.
Adjust your grip on the TRX to modify the level of assistance.

name: TRX Plank
desc: A plank variation with feet suspended in TRX straps, increasing instability and core demand.
steps: Place both feet in the TRX foot cradles.
Assume a forearm or high plank position on the floor.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Hold the position for the desired time.
Lower your knees to exit safely.
tips: Do not let your hips sag toward the floor or pike upward.
Stack your shoulders directly over your elbows or hands.
Minimize strap sway by pressing your feet gently into the cradles.

name: TRX Row
desc: This bodyweight pulling exercise uses a suspension trainer to target your entire back, building strength in the lats, rhomboids, and biceps.
steps: Grasp the handles of a suspension trainer with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
Lean back, extending your arms fully, keeping your body straight from head to heels.
Engage your core and pull your chest towards your hands, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control.
Maintain a rigid body throughout the movement, avoiding any sagging in the hips.
tips: Adjust your foot position: the closer your feet are to the anchor point, the harder the exercise.
Keep your elbows close to your body to emphasize the lats, or flare them slightly for more upper back.
Focus on initiating the pull with your back muscles, not just your arms.
Control the eccentric (lowering) phase to maximize muscle engagement.

name: TRX Side Plank
desc: A side plank with both feet suspended in TRX cradles, intensifying the demand on the obliques.
steps: Place both feet in the TRX foot cradles and lie on your side.
Prop up on your bottom forearm with your elbow under your shoulder.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line.
Stack your top foot over the bottom foot.
Hold the position while breathing steadily.
Lower and switch sides after the set.
tips: Brace your obliques before lifting your hips off the floor.
Do not let your hips drop toward the floor.
Press the forearm into the floor to keep the shoulder active.

name: TRX Squat
desc: This bodyweight compound exercise utilizes a suspension trainer to assist in performing a squat, effectively targeting the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings for lower body strength and stability.
steps: Stand facing the anchor point, holding the handles with palms facing each other, arms extended.
Lean back slightly, keeping your body straight and core engaged, with feet shoulder-width apart.
Initiate the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, lowering your body as if sitting in a chair.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor or as deep as comfortable, maintaining tension on the straps.
Drive through your heels to return to the starting position, extending your hips and knees fully.
tips: Keep your chest up and gaze forward throughout the movement to maintain a neutral spine.
Use the suspension trainer for assistance to control your descent and ascent, especially if new to squats.
Focus on pushing your knees out slightly to engage your glutes more effectively.

name: TRX Triceps Extension
desc: This exercise targets the triceps brachii using a suspension trainer, focusing on elbow extension for upper arm development and strength.
steps: Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding the TRX handles with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Lean forward, extending your arms straight out in front of you at shoulder height, creating tension in the straps.
Keeping your elbows high and fixed, bend them to lower your body by letting your hands move towards your temples.
Extend your elbows forcefully to push your body back to the starting position, squeezing your triceps.
Maintain a rigid plank position throughout the movement, engaging your core and glutes.
tips: Adjust your body angle to increase or decrease difficulty; the more horizontal, the harder the exercise.
Keep your elbows pointing forward and high to maximize triceps isolation and minimize shoulder involvement.
Control the eccentric (lowering) phase for better muscle engagement and growth.

name: TRX Y-Fly
desc: This suspension trainer exercise targets the posterior deltoids and trapezius, improving shoulder health and posture by strengthening the upper back.
steps: Stand facing the anchor point, holding the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Lean back, extending your arms straight in front of you, maintaining a plank position with your body.
Raise your arms up and out into a 'Y' overhead, pulling your shoulder blades together and down as your body rises toward the anchor.
Keep a slight, fixed bend in the elbows throughout and squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Slowly control the descent back to the starting position, resisting the pull of the straps.
tips: Adjust your body angle to modify difficulty: leaning further back increases the challenge.
Focus on retracting and depressing your shoulder blades throughout the movement.
Maintain a rigid core and straight body line to prevent sagging hips.

name: Barbell Upright Row
desc: A compound pulling movement for the lateral deltoids and upper traps.
steps: Stand holding a barbell with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Pull the bar straight up along your body toward your chin.
Lead with your elbows, keeping them above your hands.
Lower the bar with control.
Repeat.
tips: Use a lighter weight if you feel pinching in your shoulders.
Avoid bending your wrists excessively as the bar rises.
Avoid swinging or using your legs to heave the weight up.

name: Upward-Facing Dog
desc: A prone backbend on straight arms with the thighs lifted off the floor, so the arms and back extensors hold the chest open and the spine long.
steps: Lie face down with the hands beside the lower ribs and the tops of the feet on the floor.
Press the hands down and straighten the arms, lifting the chest and then the thighs off the mat.
Draw the shoulders back and down and keep the neck long.
Hold the position for the prescribed time with only the hands and the tops of the feet on the floor.
Bend the arms and lower down under control.
tips: Keep the shoulders over the wrists rather than behind them.
Press the tops of the feet down; that is what lifts the thighs.
If the thighs cannot lift, stay in cobra instead of forcing the position.

name: V-Bar Lat Pulldown
desc: A neutral-grip pulldown performed with a narrow V-handle, maximizing lat stretch and allowing a deeper contraction.
steps: Attach a V-bar (double-D handle) to a lat pulldown cable.
Sit with the thighs secured under the pad and grip the handle, palms facing each other.
Begin with the arms fully extended overhead.
Pull the handle down to the sternum by driving the elbows down and slightly back.
Squeeze the lats at the bottom, then return slowly under control.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: The neutral grip is easier on the shoulders than pronated or supinated grips.
Imagine pulling your ribs toward your hips — think lats, not arms.

name: V-Bar Tricep Pushdown
desc: A cable tricep pushdown using a V-handle, which locks the wrists in a pronated, slightly-angled position and loads the lateral head.
steps: Attach a V-bar handle to a high cable pulley.
Stand facing the stack and grip the V-bar with both hands, palms down.
Start with the elbows tucked to the sides, forearms parallel to the floor.
Press the handle down until the arms are fully extended.
Squeeze the triceps, then return under control to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the elbows pinned to the sides the entire set.
Don't lean into the bar; a small forward lean is fine, but let the triceps do the work.

name: V-Sit
desc: A static core hold balancing on the sit bones with the legs and torso lifted into a V, challenging the abdominals and hip flexors.
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you.
Lean back slightly and lift your legs off the floor.
Reach your arms forward so your body forms a V shape.
Balance on your sit bones with core tight.
Hold the position while breathing steadily.
Lower your legs and torso to exit.
tips: Keep your chest lifted and spine long rather than rounding the back.
Bend the knees if you cannot hold straight legs yet.

name: V Ups
desc: A dynamic core exercise raising the legs and torso together into a V shape, training the abs and hip flexors.
steps: Lie flat on your back with arms extended overhead and legs straight.
Simultaneously raise your legs and upper body toward each other.
Reach your hands toward your feet at the top, forming a V shape.
Keep your legs straight throughout the movement.
Lower both ends under control back to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your legs straight as you lift them.
Reach your hands toward your feet at the top.
Lower both ends under control rather than dropping flat.

name: Walking
desc: Unaided gait on level ground, keeping one foot in contact with the floor throughout, which makes it the lowest-impact way to accumulate aerobic work.
steps: Stand tall with your weight over the middle of your feet and your shoulders relaxed, not pulled back.
Step forward and land on your heel, then roll through the foot and push off the ball and toes.
Keep at least one foot on the ground at all times — as soon as both leave the floor you are running, not walking.
Let your arms swing naturally from the shoulder, opposite arm to opposite leg, with the elbows softly bent.
Look ahead rather than down at your feet, and breathe through a steady, repeatable rhythm.
Continue for the desired time or distance, picking a pace at which you could still hold a conversation.
tips: Pace is the whole variable here. A stroll and a brisk walk are different training stimuli, so pick one deliberately instead of drifting.
Lengthen the push behind you rather than reaching further in front — overstriding lands you on a straight leg and brakes every step.
This is the one piece of conditioning you can do daily without needing to recover from it, which is what makes it worth programming rather than leaving to chance.

name: Wall Ball
desc: A full-body conditioning exercise that joins a front squat and a throw: holding a soft wall ball at your chest, you squat down, drive up and throw the ball to a target high on a wall, then catch it and go straight into the next squat. The legs and hips produce the power and the arms finish the throw.
steps: Stand facing a wall about an arm's length away, feet shoulder-width apart, holding the ball at your chest with both hands.
Keep your elbows under the ball and your chest up.
Squat down until your hips are at or below knee height, keeping your heels on the floor.
Drive up hard through your legs and hips and, as you rise, throw the ball up to the target with both arms.
Catch the ball at chest height as it comes down, letting your arms absorb it.
Go straight into the next squat with the catch and repeat for the planned repetitions.
tips: Let the legs throw the ball: the push from the squat should carry it most of the way, the arms only finish the movement.
Keep your chest up and the ball close to your body in the squat so your back stays neutral.
Catch and squat in one movement; resting with the ball at the top breaks the rhythm and tires the shoulders.

name: Wall Hamstring Stretch
desc: A restful stretch for the back of the thigh: lying on your back with one leg raised and its heel resting on a wall, you let the hamstring lengthen under gravity. The wall holds the leg in place so you can relax and control the amount of stretch by how close you lie to it.
steps: Lie on your back on the floor next to a wall or an open doorway, with your hips close to the wall.
Raise one leg and rest the heel on the wall with the knee as straight as you can comfortably get it.
Keep the other leg flat on the floor and your lower back relaxed.
Shuffle your hips closer to the wall to increase the stretch, or move away to ease it.
Breathe slowly and hold for the planned time while the hamstring relaxes.
Lower the leg and repeat on the other side.
tips: Keep your tailbone on the floor; lifting it off the floor takes the stretch out of the hamstring.
A slight bend in the knee is fine; straighten it only as far as feels comfortable.
Do not strain; the stretch should feel like a long pull, not sharp pain or tingling.

name: Wall Push Ups
desc: A beginner-friendly push-up performed standing against a wall, reducing load on the chest and arms.
steps: Stand facing a wall and place your palms on it at shoulder height.
Step your feet back until your arms are fully extended.
Bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the wall.
Keep your body in a straight line throughout.
Press back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Avoid flaring your elbows straight out to the sides.
Step your feet farther from the wall to increase the difficulty.
Keep your core engaged so your hips do not sag.

name: Wall Sit
desc: A static isometric exercise holding a squat position against a wall to build quad endurance.
steps: Stand with back against a wall.
Slide down until thighs are parallel to the floor.
Hold the position.
Stand back up when done.
tips: Keep knees at 90 degrees.
Press your back flat against the wall.

name: Warrior I
desc: A split-stance standing pose with the back foot planted at an angle, the front knee bent and the arms overhead, hips facing forward.
steps: Step one foot back and turn it out about forty-five degrees, planting the whole sole.
Bend the front knee until it stacks over the ankle and keep the back leg straight.
Draw both hip points towards the front of the mat and lift the arms overhead.
Hold the position for the prescribed time with the ribs down and the chest lifted.
Step the feet together and repeat on the other side.
tips: Widen the stance sideways so both hips can face forward without straining the back knee.
Press the outer edge of the back foot down to keep the base stable.
Take the arms shoulder-width apart if bringing the palms together arches the lower back.

name: Warrior III
desc: A single-leg balance with the torso and the lifted leg parallel to the floor, forming one long line from the fingertips to the raised heel.
steps: Stand on one leg with the knee soft and the hips level.
Hinge forward from the hips as the other leg lifts behind you.
Continue until the torso and the lifted leg are roughly parallel to the floor.
Reach the arms forward, back along the body or out to the sides, and hold for the prescribed time.
Lower the leg and repeat on the other side.
tips: Keep the lifted hip from opening upwards; both hip points face the floor.
Flex the lifted foot and press the heel back to keep the leg active.
Rest the hands on blocks or a wall while you are building the balance.

name: Warrior II
desc: A wide-stance pose with the front knee bent, the hips open to the side and the arms extended in line with the shoulders.
steps: Stand wide with the front foot turned out ninety degrees and the back foot slightly in.
Bend the front knee until it stacks over the ankle and tracks towards the middle toes.
Open the hips and chest to the side and extend the arms parallel to the floor.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, gazing over the front hand.
Straighten the front leg and repeat on the other side.
tips: Keep the front knee from drifting inwards; press it towards the little-toe side.
Stack the shoulders over the hips rather than leaning towards the front leg.
Shorten the stance if the front thigh cannot get close to parallel.

name: Weighted Dips
desc: A parallel-bar dip performed with extra load — most often a plate hung from a dip belt between the legs — to keep the movement in a strength rep range once bodyweight dips are easy.
steps: Attach a plate to a dip belt around your waist so the weight hangs between your legs.
Grip the parallel dip bars and press yourself up to the top position with your arms locked out and your feet off the floor.
Lean your torso slightly forward and lower your body by bending your elbows until your shoulders are below them.
Press back up through your palms until your arms are locked out again, keeping the hanging plate from swinging.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Add weight only once you can do clean bodyweight dips through a full range — small jumps of 2.5–5 kg are enough, since the load stacks on top of your own bodyweight.
Keep your legs together and your core braced so the plate does not start swinging; a swinging weight throws off the bottom of the rep.
Keep your shoulders pulled down away from your ears and stop the descent if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder.

name: Weighted Pull-Up
desc: A pull-up performed with extra load — most often a plate hung from a dip belt between the legs — to keep the movement in a strength rep range once bodyweight pull-ups are easy.
steps: Attach a plate to a dip belt around your waist so the weight hangs between your legs, or hold the load between your feet.
Grip the pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width and hang at full arm extension with your legs together.
Pull your elbows down and back to drive your chest toward the bar until your chin clears it.
Lower yourself under control back to the full dead hang, keeping tension on your lats and letting the weight settle before the next rep.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Add weight only once you can do clean bodyweight pull-ups through a full range — small jumps of 2.5–5 kg are enough, since the load stacks on top of your own bodyweight.
Keep your legs together and your core braced so the hanging plate does not start swinging; a swinging weight turns the rep into a kip.
Do not cut the bottom short — return to a full dead hang each rep, and stop the set when your chin stops clearing the bar rather than grinding out partials.

name: Weighted Wall Crunch
desc: A crunch variation with the legs parked out of the way -- feet braced against a wall or box, or the legs simply held up -- so the hips stay quiet and the abs do the work.
steps: Lie on your back and park your legs so your hips cannot help: brace your feet against a wall or a box, or hold your legs up with the knees bent.
Hold a weight against your chest with both hands -- a plate, a dumbbell, or a kettlebell all work.
Crunch up, lifting your shoulder blades off the floor.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
tips: Exhale as you crunch up and inhale on the way down.
Keep your neck relaxed instead of pulling your head forward.
Press your lower back into the floor throughout the movement.

name: Wide-Grip Bench Press
desc: A bench press variation with a wider-than-shoulder-width grip to maximize chest activation.
steps: Lie on a flat bench. Grip the barbell wider than shoulder-width.
Lower the bar to mid-chest.
Press back up to full extension.
Repeat.
tips: A wider grip reduces triceps involvement.
Avoid excessive wrist bending.

name: Wide Grip Pull Ups
desc: A pull-up performed with a wide overhand grip, emphasizing the lats and upper-back width.
steps: Grip the pull-up bar with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width.
Hang with arms fully extended and core braced.
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down.
Keep your shoulders pulled back as you rise.
Lower yourself under control to full extension.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Initiate each rep by depressing your shoulder blades before bending the arms.
Avoid kipping or swinging your legs for momentum.
Squeeze the bar firmly and keep your wrists straight.

name: Wide Grip Push Ups
desc: A push-up variation with a wider hand placement to emphasize the chest.
steps: Start in a high plank with hands wider than shoulder-width.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Keep your core braced and glutes engaged.
Press back up until your arms are extended.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your elbows at roughly 45 degrees from your torso.
Maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Lower until your chest is close to the floor.

name: Wide Grip Seated Cable Row
desc: A seated rowing variation with a wide grip emphasizing the upper back.
steps: Sit at a cable row station with feet on the platform.
Grip a wide bar with an overhand grip.
Pull the bar toward your upper abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Extend your arms back to the starting position with control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid rocking back and forth.
Drive your elbows high and wide to target the upper back.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees throughout the set.

name: Wide-Legged Forward Fold
desc: A standing fold from a wide stance with the hands on the floor, lengthening the hamstrings and the inner thighs while the spine hangs long.
steps: Stand with the feet wide apart and the outer edges parallel.
Place the hands on the hips, lift the chest and hinge forward from the hip joints.
Bring the hands to the floor under the shoulders and let the head hang.
Hold the fold for the prescribed time, shifting the weight slightly into the balls of the feet.
Bring the hands back to the hips and come up with a flat back.
tips: Micro-bend the knees so the fold comes from the hips rather than the lower back.
Keep the feet parallel; turning them out takes the stretch out of the inner thighs.
Rest the hands on blocks when the floor is out of reach.

name: Wide-Stance Leg Press
desc: A leg press with a wide, slightly turned-out stance that increases the contribution of the adductors alongside hip and knee extension while the back stays supported.
steps: Set the back pad and seat so your lower back remains supported at the bottom of the repetition.
Place your feet wide on the platform with the toes turned out only as far as the knees can follow comfortably.
Lower the sled by bending the hips and knees while keeping the knees aligned with the toes and the feet flat.
Press through the whole foot and extend the hips and knees without forcing the knees into lockout.
Lower the sled under control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a width and toe angle that your hips can control; wider is not automatically better.
Keep the knees moving in the same direction as the toes rather than letting them collapse inward.
Stop the descent before the pelvis rolls under and the lower back loses contact with the pad.

name: World's Greatest Stretch
desc: A flowing mobility drill that combines a deep lunge with a trunk rotation. From a low lunge with both hands on the floor, you turn your chest toward the front leg and reach one arm to the ceiling, opening the hips, the upper back and the shoulder in one movement.
steps: Start in a push-up position with your hands under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Step one foot forward, outside the same-side hand, into a deep lunge and keep the back leg straight.
Keep the hand on the back-leg side planted under your shoulder and sink your hips toward the floor.
Rotate your chest toward the front leg, lifting the arm on that side up until it points at the ceiling, and follow your hand with your eyes.
Hold the open position for a breath, then lower your hand back to the floor.
Step back to the push-up position and repeat on the other side, alternating sides for the planned repetitions.
tips: Keep the back knee off the floor and the back leg active so the stretch runs through the front of the hip.
Rotate from the upper back rather than leaning sideways; the hips stay square and low throughout.
Move slowly and breathe out as you rotate; the stretch should feel open and controlled, never forced.

name: Bilateral Dumbbell Wrist Curl
desc: A dumbbell wrist curl performed with both arms at once, isolating the forearm flexors for a time-efficient forearm session.
steps: Sit on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, forearms resting on your thighs, palms up.
Let both dumbbells roll down to your fingertips.
Curl both dumbbells up by flexing your wrists.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your forearms pinned to your thighs throughout -- only the wrists move.
Use a lighter load per hand than you would single-arm, since both sides work simultaneously.

name: Wrist Roller
desc: A forearm exercise winding a hanging weight up and down a roller, building grip and wrist strength.
steps: Grip the wrist roller handle with arms extended in front at shoulder height.
Let the weight hang from the cord.
Roll the handle forward with alternating wrist movements to wind the weight up.
Keep your arms straight throughout.
Once fully wound, reverse the rotation to lower the weight.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Use full wrist rotations rather than small partial turns.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging as you roll.
Control the unwinding phase instead of letting the weight drop.

name: Zercher Squat
desc: A squat in which the barbell is held in the crooks of the elbows at the front of the body. The front-loaded bar keeps the torso upright and works the quadriceps, glutes, upper back and core.
steps: Set a barbell in a rack at about waist height, step in and hook it into the crooks of the elbows, with the forearms crossed or the hands clasped in front of the chest.
Lift the bar out of the rack, step back and stand with the feet about shoulder-width apart.
Brace the core and keep the chest up and the elbows pressed together.
Squat down by bending the hips and knees until the thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through the middle of the feet to stand back up.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then re-rack the bar.
tips: Wrap the bar in a pad or towel; the elbow crease is sensitive and can bruise.
Keep the elbows high and together so the bar does not roll toward the hands.
Keep the torso upright; if the chest drops, lower the load.

name: Zottman Curl
desc: A standing dumbbell curl that lifts with a supinated grip, rotates to palms-down at the top, and lowers in pronation to combine biceps work with a forearm-heavy eccentric.
steps: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, arms extended at your sides, and a dumbbell in each hand with the palms facing forward.
Keep your upper arms beside your ribs and curl both dumbbells toward your shoulders without swinging the torso.
At the top, keep the elbows bent and rotate the forearms until the palms face down.
Lower the dumbbells slowly with the pronated grip until the arms are straight.
Turn the palms forward again at the bottom and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use less weight than for a standard dumbbell curl; the palms-down lowering phase is usually the limiting part.
Rotate through the forearms while keeping the wrists straight rather than bending them around the handles.
Keep the elbows close to the ribs and avoid turning the curl into a shoulder swing.
